title: Type a number, then click — and both are gone
item: A field's change handler rebuilds the DOM under the pointer, so the value you typed never lands and the control you aimed at is destroyed between mousedown and click. In the devices flow the change handler calls a full render; on the manifest a row field's change replaces the whole summary block, taking the labor-rate input with it. It looks random because a field left unchanged tabs fine, and the buffer is safe — only the user's next action is lost.
evidence: device.js:283-286 calls TakeoffApp.render() on every change; manifest.js:167 replaces .manifest-summary via outerHTML. A straight-through Tab pass over three device rows saved a bid with Devices material $0.00 (true $175.00); one click each on Save / + Box / PB / trash / x2 immediately after typing did nothing (J4 NEW-1). On the manifest 4/4 first clicks on Labor Rate were swallowed - focus to <body>, field empty, Labor Total $0.00 instead of $160.86; a 2 s pause does not help and the summary node identity provably changes on the row field's change.
proposal: Delete the render() from the device flow's change (J4 P1) and stop the row field's change rebuilding a summary block its own input handler already patched; bind the labor rate once by delegation, patch cells in place and restore focus (J1 P1 = J8 P12 - ship once). Verifier confirmed nothing reads a re-rendered value, so only cosmetic re-normalisation of typed text is lost; the conduit/wire half of J4 P1 is a no-op and drops out.
event: field_commit_lost (debug counter during bake-in) + flow_saved {kind, rows, componentPrice}

title: An assembly lands on the bid at a different price than the row you clicked
item: addAssemblyEntry explodes an MC assembly into its components whenever a composition exists - and all 24,291 entries have one - so the components' prices replace the book price the BOM footer just promised. The rolled-up branch is unreachable outside fill mode, which means README's 'rolled-up or exploded' describes a choice that does not exist. Unpriced components are stored as the number 0 rather than null, so the purchase list counts them as priced and its 'n without a price' flag goes quiet on exactly the gap this creates.
evidence: mcBook.js:259-262; renderBom only relabels (:150-153). 100A ENCL CB 2P 250V - row 4.03 hrs / $193.65, footer 'using the book price' - added onto a x3 panel as $2.76 and 5.70 hrs, -99.5% against $580.95. Coupling row $1.66 - child $0.76 (-54%). Whole-book scan: component-sum / book-price median 1.099, p90 18.7; 5,179 priced entries explode to under half their book price. J6 NEW-1: after the add the list carried '100A CIRCUIT TERM x 18 - $0.00' as a priced line.
proposal: J6 P1 as reshaped by verifier: explode only when the components reconstruct the book price within a tolerance, otherwise add the rolled-up entry at the book's labor and price, and flash what happened ('Added 20A ENCL CB 2P 250V - 1.7 hrs - $57.34, book price'). The walker's 'unpriced === 0' test is insufficient - the fully priced #12 MTR TERM still explodes $42.52 to $23.88. Store unpriced components as null, not 0. Fill mode is unchanged and the single undo frame survives.

title: A part added to a 220-ft run arrives 220 times
item: inheritedQty and scale apply the parent's quantity to every item type, so a run's footage becomes a part count. The same part added from inside the conduit wizard arrives once, so two doors on one row disagree in silence - and the banner on the door that adds one is the door that says 'x220 on the bid'. Inside that single wizard door a single entry lands qty 1 while an assembly's components land at the run's footage.
evidence: laborBookTargets.js:102-105 (manifest door), :176 and :186 (scale), :99 (wizard door = qty 1). A 145-ft feeder took an Elliot coupling at x145 @ $73.0758 = $10,595.99; the same part added inside the wizard landed qty 1. The walker's 220-ft case: x220 couplings = $233.20 (assembly) + $1,794.91 (Elliot) on one run. J6 NEW-3 measured the split inside the fittings door.
proposal: J6 P2 with the verifier's scope correction: inherit a quantity only when the parent's type is gear, lighting, devices or specialSystems; conduit and wire parents get 1, and the flash reads 'Added x1 under 3/4" EMT Homerun - set the count'. The rule must cover addComponentsToTarget's fittings branch (:186) as well as the manifest branch (:176), or the wizard keeps the bug the proposal names.

title: "Add All" on a re-count duplicates every fixture you already have
item: Import counts are totals, and the more prominent of the two buttons treats them as additions. On a re-count Add All appends a second, untyped, unpriced row for every fixture that already exists - so the manifest over-counts while the summary does not move, because the new rows carry no price. The purchase list then merges the two rows' quantities but only the priced row's extended cost, producing a line whose qty times unit does not equal its extended.
evidence: import.js:101-133; index.html:232-233 - both buttons are .btn-success, Add All sits rightmost and README lists it first. Seed Troffer 24 @ $89.50 + import 30 gives 54 troffers for a count of 30, Lighting stays $3,660.00 (should be $4,197.00), purchase list prints '54 | $89.50 | $2148.00' where 54 x 89.50 = $4,833. selectors.js:76-82 sums quantity for every occurrence and extended only for priced ones; the row is greyed, with no title and no marker. No confirm and no delta-aware button state exists anywhere in the code.
proposal: J2 P1: one state-aware primary button - empty manifest 'Add 5 fixtures', anything matched 'Update 1 count - add 2 fixtures' (today's Add-Overages-Only behaviour); demote Add All to a secondary 'Add as separate rows', shown only when at least one line matched. Makes the duplicate outcome unreachable by a single click and retires the word 'overage' from this modal. The verifier noted the label can carry the receipt for free, which is where J2 P7's value belongs.

title: A row at quantity 0 still bills once — and disappears from the purchase list
item: Two deliberate, separately tested rules contradict each other on the same row: the summary treats a priced row at quantity 0 as one unit, while the purchase list drops any row at quantity 0. Zeroing a row is the most common what-if in a bid check, and it shows the job with the row still in it, at one unit, plus the hours to install one - then the two reports disagree by exactly that unit price. Inside the flows it leaks to components, where the rule was never intended.
evidence: selectors.js:145/148 (effectiveQty = qty > 0 ? qty : price > 0 ? 1 : 0, pinned at selectors.test.js:15) against selectors.js:69 (if (!desc || qty <= 0) return). Panel LP-2 ($980 / 6.5 h) spun to 0: Gear still $981.85 / 6.5 hrs; regenerated list '14 materials' $6,826.15 against Sub Total $7,806.15 - delta exactly $980.00. A PB-filled fitting at qty 0 / $58.4697 added $58.47 to Conduit while the list skipped it: Sub Total $5,824.74 vs footer $5,766.27.
proposal: J8 P2 owns it: drop the counts-once branch so quantity 0 contributes 0 to materials, labor and the list and the three agree by construction; keep 'typing a description sets qty 1' (manifest.js:383) so the case the rule protected stays visible as 1; grey the qty cell on a described, priced row at 0. J5 P7's component-only split is subsumed. Update selectors.test.js:15. This is an owner decision - it changes the totals of existing bids.
event: qty_zero_priced_row (fires on save; measures the rule's real frequency before and after)

title: Undo runs first and asks afterwards — "Cancel" doesn't cancel
item: The header's Undo handler calls TakeoffState.undo() and only then navigates, which raises the discard prompt. Answering Cancel leaves the editor open over a manifest that has already moved, on a row the estimator was not even looking at; saving then writes the buffer onto the undone manifest and clears Redo, so the change is unrecoverable. Redo has the identical defect, and its variant restores a child the open buffer never hydrated, which the next Save deletes again.
evidence: app.js:336-340 (Undo), :343-347 (Redo). Conduit: a saved 10% overage (15 ft @ $1.10) on the bid with the flow dirty at 15% - Undo, Cancel - view still conduit, the overage child gone, Conduit $181.50 to $165.00, and the next Save wrote 23 ft, a third number. Devices: plan page E3.9 to E3.1 under an open editor, then 'Save and Back' wrote onto the undone manifest and cleared Redo so E3.9 could not be recovered by exhausting Redo. Severity reconciled to blocker - J3 rated it stumble, J5 blocker - because the loss is silent and Redo cannot undo it.
proposal: J3 P6 = J5 P1, one item and one plan of record, not to be scheduled twice: run the existing 'Discard unsaved changes in this editor?' confirm before undo()/redo() and return on Cancel. Three lines each, and the Redo lines are not optional (J5 NEW-3).

title: The discard guard has three holes, and the only exit from steps 2–3 goes through one
item: Baseline B-3 installed a 'Discard unsaved changes?' guard on the flow editors. The conduit wizard defeats it three ways: goToStep clears flowDirty on backward moves although only forward moves commit; book-side adds into the fittings buffer never set the flag at all; and steps 2 and 3 render no Cancel, so Back-then-Cancel is the only Cancel route and it never asks. This is a hole in B-3's fix, not a re-report of it.
evidence: conduit.js:117-126 (goToStep clears on backward), :263-266 and :286-289 (no Cancel on steps 2-3), :206 (the only Cancel). A typed fitting 3 x 0.12 x 2.40 - Back - Cancel gave 0 dialogs and the row was gone. grep setFlowDirty finds no call in any book module, so a book-added hanger was discarded with no confirm even via the guarded app-title route. Dialogs were driven in dismiss mode so a confirm would actually have blocked the exit.
proposal: J5 P3: make Next, Back and the step pills pure navigation and write trench, add-ons, fittings and overage in one batch on Save - the wire flow already works this way. That removes commitStep1/commitStep2's mid-wizard writes (~60 lines), the 'Trenching: 0 - N/A @ N/A' child on every non-trenched run, two of the three undo frames per run and both Back/Cancel special cases; put a Cancel on every step while you are there. J6 P12's setFlowDirty half is subsumed - it does not close the hole on its own, because goToStep still disarms the flag.

title: Component quantities are totals for the whole run, and nothing says so
item: Every component row in the devices flow is seeded Quantity 1 beside a panel that says the run is Quantity 20, and the saved child is added to the bid as quantity times price with no multiplication by the run count. Read the box as per-run and the line prices 20x under; read it as a total and it is right. Nothing on the screen declares which, and the app's other door states the opposite rule out loud.
evidence: device.js:186 (hasParentDesc ? 1 : quantity), also app.js:133, device.js:255/375; selectors.js multiplies nothing by the run count. Three rows read as totals give $175.00 / 9.2 hrs; read as per-run they give $8.75 / 0.46 hrs - 20x under, and both look right. The manifest row's book door banners 'Adding parts under: ... x20 on the bid' (laborBook.js:360) while the flow seeds the opposite value with no label. Pressing D in the type modal drops a first-timer straight into this on the fastest path in.
proposal: J4 P2: seed every component row with the parent's quantity, head the column 'Quantity (all 20 runs)' and add the panel line 'Price: $175.00 - $8.75 per run'. Keeps the storage model, deletes the hasParentDesc ternary in four places and closes the flow-versus-book split. Regression checked: isMeaningfulRow ignores quantity, so seeded blank rows still stay out of the totals and out of the save.

title: A saved assembly is a snapshot of one run's counts, not a recipe
item: Save as Assembly stores absolute quantities, so loading the preset onto a line with a different run count carries the old counts. The reuse feature's whole point is 'same recipe, different count'; today every load needs four quantities retyped, and forgetting is invisible because the card prints a dollar figure with no 'per what'.
evidence: A preset saved from a 20-run line loaded onto an 8-run line stays 20/20/20: panel $175.00, saved bid Devices $350.00 for 28 runs, purchase list '40 - Decora receptacle'. Per-run-correct for the 8-run line is $70.00. No warning anywhere; the card title says 'Extended material price (qty x unit)' and nothing else.
proposal: J4 P3 with the verifier's required amendment: store the ratio and round up at load. A plain divide-then-multiply manufactures fractional part counts - a qty-1 support on 20 runs stores 0.05 and loads onto 8 runs as 0.4, and neither getPurchaseList nor getSummaryBreakdown rounds, so the list would read '0.4 - CADDY box support'. Card reads '$8.75 per run - 0.46 hrs per run - 4 parts'; flag stored assemblies perRun and load legacy ones as today with a note. The flag must survive the cloud merge, since takeoff-assemblies merges as a union.

title: Money typed the way estimators write it is stored as text and prices at $0
item: A price typed with a dollar sign or a comma is stored verbatim as a string. The book stamps it 'You - today', the row looks priced, and the same part lands on the bid as $0 because the manifest's number input renders the string blank - while its labor hours still count. The literal string would also ride into the shared book as a correction.
evidence: state.js:549-571 never coerces; laborBook.js:519 passes the raw string. '$21,450.75' on a Switchboards row: badge 'You - today', child on the bid price:"$21,450.75" with a blank number input, materials +$0 but labor +30 hrs, purchase list '1200a Switchboards - unpriced', and getBookCorrections carrying the string. '1,975' and '5,000.00' become NaN the same way; ' 2400 ' survives only because addRowToFixture trims.
proposal: J7 P1: one parser on the way in - strip $, commas and spaces; if the result is not finite keep the field text, store price:'' and do not stamp provenance, and outline the field. The verifier's binding caveat: it must also cover the catalog price input (laborBookElliot.js:192) and the corrections shape, or the string still reaches J12.

title: Recording a quote on the fixture's own part, then adding it, double-counts the fixture
item: From a manifest row's book icon the only door is 'add a part underneath', so a quoted part lands beside the price it was meant to replace instead of correcting it. There is no warning that the fixture already carries a price and no fill affordance on any manifest row - even though the code path for exactly that has been built, is advertised in README, and has zero callers.
evidence: SWBD-1 ($18,400 / 30 hrs) plus an Add of book row '1200a' ($17,995 / 30 hrs) took gear materials $20,800 to $38,795 and gear labor 66 to 96 hrs, with no warning of any kind. J7 NEW-1: TakeoffApp.showPartBookSearchForManifestItem -> {kind:'manifest-row'} -> addEntryToTarget (laborBookTargets.js:37-38) with a banner label already mapped at laborBook.js:339, and no caller anywhere. One undo does recover.
proposal: J7 P3 as reshaped by verifier, and cheaper than it looks: when the book is opened from a top-level row that has its own price and no children, Add on a curated row of the fixture's own type defaults to 'Use as Panel A's price' - price and labor replaced, provenance carried onto the manifest row - with 'Add as a part underneath' demoted to the banner's secondary action. Wires the existing dead path; PB flows are untouched because they route through the same function by a different fill.kind. One caveat: the manifest-row branch overwrites description, so pass a flag rather than changing the shared branch.

title: The purchase list freezes the moment you start correcting the bid
item: Inline edits patch only the summary block, so an open purchase list is left as it was. The two artifacts the estimator is reconciling disagree because they are being reconciled, on one screen, and copying at that moment sends the old list to the supply house. The data is correct throughout - it is the DOM that never re-renders.
evidence: updateSummaryOnly() (manifest.js:395, :411, :424) replaces only .manifest-summary (:165-167). Box 15 to 25, typed and tabbed, with the list open: summary Sub Total $7,825.65 above a list still reading $7,806.15 and a box row still saying 15, while TakeoffState.getPurchaseList().totalCost was already 7825.65. Refreshes only on a full render; the walker's claim that tabbing out of the labor rate refreshes it is wrong after any inline edit, because the swapped listener patches in place (list $2,227.50 vs fresh $2,301.75).
proposal: J8 P1: updateSummaryOnly() also re-renders the open purchase list and re-binds Copy/Hide, with the same outerHTML patch. It must fire from the swapped labor-rate listener (manifest.js:168-171) too - that is the path where the stale list survives today.

title: The purchase list merges by description, so lines arrive that don't multiply — or can't be ordered
item: getPurchaseList merges on description alone. Three consequences reach the supply house: two rows of one fixture at different prices merge into a line whose quantity times unit does not equal its extended; two curated fitting rows that share a bare name (an elbow and a coupling) merge into one unorderable line; and every run's overage carries the same description, so two runs' waste merges into a quantity of an abstraction while the buyable footage line still reads the un-wasted number.
evidence: selectors.js:60-63. (a) '2 - Panel LP-2 != - $980.00 - $1830.00' where 2 x 980 = 1,960; the explanation is a title on a 14.4 px glyph and the TSV drops the glyph entirely. (b) 10 of 10 row names shared between EMT fittings (SS) Elbows and (SS) - Couplings; describeBookRow appends the section only under 10 characters (laborBookTargets.js:19), so 1" EMT(R) at 9 chars gets its section and 1/2" EMT(S) at 11 does not - adding one of each produced '1/2" EMT(S) x 6'. (c) '23 - Conduit overage (10%) != - $1.12 - $22.24' across two runs, and a single run reads '15 - Conduit overage (10%)' beside an EMT line saying 150, not 165 (conduit.js:522, wire.js:151).
proposal: Three coordinated changes in one file. J6 P3: delete the name.length < 10 rule rather than re-tuning it - length is a proxy for nothing - and always append the section kind ('3/4" EMT(S) coupling'); the same describe path feeds fill mode and the flow rows. J8 P4: a varying price renders as a range ($1100.00-$1250.00) in the cell and the TSV, and the != glyph and its tooltip go (Extended $ stays numeric, which is the column that gets summed). J8 P5: overage children fold into the parent's line by parentId plus type, never by description ('242 - 3/4" EMT Homerun (incl. 10% overage)'), with wire identical and a null-priced overage folding as unpriced quantity.

title: Clicking a row's trash shows the confirm, takes the OK, and removes nothing
item: The remove handler reads e.target.dataset.id, and the target of a click at the button's centre is the <path> inside its SVG. The confirm fires, OK is accepted, and nothing is removed - no row, no undo frame. Only the button's 4 px padding ring, or Enter on the focused button, carries the id. A confirmed OK that does nothing reads as 'delete is broken' and drives estimators to the quantity-0 workaround, which is its own wrong number.
evidence: manifest.js:463-465. locator.click() at the 24x24 button's centre: dialog 'Remove this item?', OK accepted, top-level rows 6 to 6, canUndo() false (0 frames), elementFromPoint returns <path> with dataset.id undefined. A raw mouse click 2 px inside the corner, click({position:{x:2,y:2}}) and focus+Enter each removed. 8 of 8 in the walk, 1 of 1 re-driven. No closest( anywhere in manifest.js, no pointer-events guard, and every sibling handler that works already uses e.currentTarget.
proposal: J3 P1: e.currentTarget.dataset.id, and make the same edit at manifest.js:431 (.select-type-btn) and :437 (.clear-type-btn), which work today only because their content is a bare text node and break the day either grows an icon. The Playwright case must click the icon's centre - that is exactly the failing case.

title: The share link carries the bid but not the labor rate
item: The share envelope has no laborRate, so the recipient's new project inherits whichever rate their own device happened to be carrying. Two people read the same bid and see different grand totals, with nothing on either screen explaining why. A recipient whose own rate is non-zero is the worse case, because there is no visible 0 to notice.
evidence: app.js:314-320 - envelope keys are exactly v, app, exportedAt, name, manifest. One bid, three grand totals: sender at $92 $4,402.98; fresh-profile recipient (rate 0) $2,056.97; a recipient whose own bid carried $60/hr $3,586.97. createProject deliberately carries the open project's rate (state.js:282-283), which the verifier judged makes the wrong number harder to spot rather than less wrong.
proposal: J9 P1 = J10 P3's envelope half, landed as one change: put laborRate in the envelope and call setLaborRate after createProject, only when typeof data.laborRate === 'number' so legacy links keep today's behaviour. Acceptance: a recipient whose own rate is 60 sees 92 on the shared copy and still 60 on their own bid. J10's 'shop rate as an account default' half is optional polish and must not hold this up.

title: The one PDF meant for a reviewer is unreadable, and its hours are wrong
item: Print for Review lays out fixed column widths that are far too narrow for 10 pt text, so descriptions run through the Quantity and Labor columns and the header itself overlaps. Labor prints to one decimal per unit, so the per-foot rates of conduit and wire round to 0.0 and the reviewer is told the wire is free to pull. And the document called Review carries no dollar figure at all - no extended cost, no materials, no tax, no grand total.
evidence: pdf.js:36 lays 25/80/35/35/40/35 pt columns; measured with jsPDF's own getTextWidth on a 44-row bid, 44 of 44 descriptions cross Quantity (x=145), 39 cross Labor, and the bold header 'Plan Page / Location' is 97.4 pt and overruns 'Price' by 57.4 pt. pdf.js:57 rounds labor: 0.04 to '0.0' and 0.006 to '0.0', so the wire and conduit runs - 25.2 of 139 hrs - print as free while 'Total Labor: 139.0 hrs' is right. No $, 'Materials', 'Tax' or 'Grand' text run exists anywhere in either PDF. J9 NEW-1: the Type column prints the raw internal key cut to 8 characters (outletsA, trenchin, powerCoC) while manifest.js:10-35 already owns display labels.
proposal: J9 P2: page 1 is the summary the screen already shows, with $ and cents; then the table with measured column widths, labor at two decimals, extended labor and extended price columns, children indented, and the existing TYPE_LABELS / CHILD_TYPE_LABELS map instead of raw keys. The proposal's own fixed widths sum to 525 of 532 pt with no gutters, so measure rather than fix them; the verifier's longest 45-char description was 195.9 pt at 10 pt, so a 220 pt description column holds. 'Makes the filename confusion unnecessary' is overclaimed - filenames are B10's job.

title: Switching bids from inside a flow editor lands on a blank page — or writes into the wrong bid
item: Switching projects while a flow editor is open swaps the manifest but leaves the view and the old project's item id in place, so the editor renders nothing: a header over an empty page with no control on it, no dialog, and no recovery that does not throw the edit away. Worse, a duplicated or shared bid carries the same item ids as its source, so switching to a twin does not blank the page - the editor re-renders on the twin and Save writes the unsaved row into the wrong bid, silently, under a header showing the right-looking name.
evidence: projects.js:69-74 switches without leaving the view; TakeoffDeviceView.render returns '' for an unknown item (device.js:61-62). All twelve combinations (device x conduit x wire x dirty/clean x switcher and Manage->Open) end with #main-content innerHTML.length 0, zero dialogs, Esc and Undo/Redo dead, and the Labor & Price Book listing only the new bid's fixtures. J10 F1b: sanitizeImportedItem keeps any well-formed raw.id (state.js:55) and duplicateProject clones ids verbatim (state.js:303-309) - row 'MEANT-FOR-ALPHA' typed on Alpha, switched to Alpha (copy), Saved: Alpha's children [], the copy's ['MEANT-FOR-ALPHA']. J10 F1c: creating a bid from the blank page leaves you on the blank page, because createProject never resets currentView/currentItemId either.
proposal: J10 P1 with the verifier's promotion: switchTo, createFromRow, the header-menu New Project path and Manage->Open all call navigateToManifest() first - it already asks when dirty - and abort the switch if the user keeps their edits; and TakeoffApp.render falls back to the manifest when a flow's item is missing (app.js:15-24). That second half is required, not defensive: without it the twin case silently succeeds. Consider re-id'ing on duplicate and on #d= import as belt and braces.

title: The supplier price update deletes the catalog and advises publishing that
item: Processing the bundled price file builds an overlay larger than a self-imposed size cap, so it is stored with its new-item list emptied - and patchLaborBook then reads 'no new items' as 'remove every supplier section', stripping the whole committed catalog from every tab, immediately and after every reload. The downloaded book carries the same emptiness, and the warning beside the download buttons tells the maintainer to commit it so the prices are kept. The Assemblies status reports the loss as success. Recovery exists but nothing points to it, and it silently discards the review queue.
evidence: The bundled CSV builds a 2,718,636-char overlay against MAX_BYTES = 2500000 (mcElliotState.js:10); saveOverlay (:136-144) stores 2,885 chars with newItems: [] and newItemsTruncated: true; the else-branch at elliotPriceCore.js:445-449 then filters every supplier section out. Measured twice in fresh profiles: 13 sections / 27,556 parts to 0 on all six tabs, with the book re-fetched and no reload, and again after reload. Downloaded mc-labor-book.json 4,063,536 B against 7,786,102 B committed, 0 supplier sections, meta.elliot.newItems 0. labor-book.spec.js:20 passes in the broken state. J13 NEW-2: the warning blames local storage, which is false - Chrome stored the full payload with no quota error. J13 NEW-3: every overlay re-save (each Match, each category change) goes back through the same cap. J13 NEW-1: 'Remove overlay' also deletes the 847 KB / 2,525-row review queue while promising confirmations are kept.
proposal: J13 P1 as reshaped by verifier. Guard (i) is load-bearing and ships regardless: patchLaborBook must treat 'no new items' as leave the committed catalog alone, never as remove it - this alone makes the catalog un-losable and also closes NEW-3, which a diet does not. Guard (ii): downloadPatchedBook refuses when the patched book has fewer supplier entries than the fetched one. (iii) drop the cap or move the overlay to IndexedDB rather than dieting - the tab-mapped-only diet measures 2,278,974 chars, 8.8% of headroom, which one bigger Elliot file erases. Fix the false warning copy and make Remove overlay say what it deletes.
event: supplier_file_processed {rows, matched, review, truncated} + catalog_sections_rendered {tab, count} — the cheapest possible alarm

title: Auto-matching overwrites saved mappings and prices two MC items from one supplier SKU
item: The item-mapping store is keyed by supplier part number, so when the automatic pass guesses a part number that is already mapped to a different MC item, the newest guess wins and the saved match is replaced with no signal. Because the map is one-to-one by part number, the same supplier SKU ends up pricing two different MC items in the live overlay, and the mapping file flips back and forth on every upload.
evidence: setMapping keys by part number (mcElliotState.js:123-128); runMatching applies saved mappings first, then lets the auto pass overwrite the same key. The downloaded file and the committed elliot-item-mappings.json are both 173 entries with exactly four differences - 1709 8706->8732, 1711 8708->8734, 1713 8710->8736, 813400 26452->26453 - and a second import in the same session flipped all four back. Live in the overlay, not just the file: 8706 (die-cast) and 8732 (non-die-cast) both at $4.3233, and a 3/4 x 8' ground rod carrying the 10' rod's $35.18. The summary shows '4 matched automatically' with no hint they replaced anything, and the mapping count stays 173.
proposal: J13 P2: when an auto match's part number already maps to a different MC item, push it to the review queue with the saved match shown as the current answer and count it separately ('4 matched automatically - 0 replaced saved matches'). The verifier's binding addition: the fix must also stop one Elliot part pricing two MC items in a single overlay, which is where the wrong dollars actually land. Note the committed 173 are apply-elliot-prices.js --match output, not human confirmations, so the severity rests on the prices, not on 'deliberately mapped'.

title: Two shipped default rows share a name, and the merge is name-keyed
item: The Labor & Price Book's whole provenance model matches rows by name, and the shipped defaults contain one duplicate name inside one section. So every version bump silently rewrites an untouched default to the other row's hours, the merge never settles, pre-versioning users get a phantom correction they never made, and on one reachable path two corrections carry the identical conflict key - which Postgres rejects, so the whole push fails behind a console warning while the dialog says N corrections shared.
evidence: laborBookDefaults.js:575-576 ships two rows named PVC GLUE in section PVC GLUE at 15 hrs and 5 hrs - exactly one duplicate in all 481 default rows. laborBookMerge.js matches on r.name === def.name (:47, :58, :88, :102, :126). mergeDefaults(pristine book, identical defaults) returns changed = 1, 2, 2, 2 over four calls and never settles, because the 15-hr row is rewritten 5->15->5 inside every call. bootstrap then flags the 5-hr row edited and computeCorrections emits a phantom 'PVC GLUE 15 -> 5'; on the merge-then-bootstrap path two rows carry the same (user_id, tab, section, part_name) key and cloud.js:433-435 swallows the rejection.
proposal: J12 P1: fix the data (two names or one row), add the assertion the suite already makes against a synthetic fixture - mergeDefaults(clone(LABOR_BOOK_DEFAULTS), LABOR_BOOK_DEFAULTS, {}) === 0, which is laborBookMerge.test.js:90's invariant and fails on the real data today - and make the merge refuse (or index-match) a section carrying duplicate names. Blocks T2-11 and part of B14: the 'N values changed' line prints an inflated count and 'equals the shipped default' is undefined until this lands.

title: Two devices on one bid overwrite each other silently, with ✓ on both
item: There is no realtime and no polling - a device reconciles once per page load or when Sync Now is pressed - and a push upserts the whole project row with the client's own clock as updated_at, without ever consulting the remote. So the second device overwrites the first on its own push, before any reconcile, with no field merge, no conflict copy and no notice; adopting a remote project then clears the local undo stack, so nothing can bring the lost version back. Last-write-wins is a documented design fact; what this row rests on is silent, unrecoverable, and a checkmark on both machines.
evidence: syncDown runs once per load (syncedThisLoad, cloud.js:521-524); pushProjectNow (:263-269) upserts the whole row with updated_at: project.savedAt; adoptProject clears undo (state.js:234-236). No realtime, no channel(, no setInterval and no keepalive anywhere in the repo. setStatus('syncing') appears only at cloud.js:78, so neither queuePush nor queueProjectPush changes the status and the checkmark lies for the whole 1.2 s debounce plus network time - exactly the lid-close window. Cloud interior is a wall: code-verified line by line, never signed in.
proposal: J11 P8 with the verifier's binding extension: when syncProjects would replace a local project whose savedAt is within the session or whose manifest differs, keep the loser as '<name> (conflict - <device time>)' in the same account and show a one-line header notice; and put an updated_at precondition on the push, or the earlier copy is already gone from the cloud before anyone reconciles. Reject any version that adds a merge dialog - the point is keep both, say so. The status half (J11 #13) ships with B13.

title: On a phone the book shows everything about a part except what it is
item: Two surfaces, two mechanisms, one outcome: at phone widths the Labor & Price Book renders parts you cannot identify. Supplier catalog rows are a seven-column table with no minimum width inside an overflow:hidden section, so the name is clipped to three characters and nothing pans - a full ancestor audit found no element a finger can scroll. And in global search the part name is the only shrinkable item in a flex row, so it collapses to zero width while the context and prices stay - which also kills the workaround the tablet dossier itself recommended.
evidence: At 375 px the catalog table is 467 px (right edge 513) inside .labor-book-section { overflow: hidden } (styles.css:1311), clipping at x~363: Name 38.2 px = 3 of 27 characters, Part # 26.8 px, Price 33.4 px, the provenance badge at x 366-484 hit-testing as DIV.modal. A 400 px horizontal wheel leaves every scrollLeft at 0 and window.scrollTo(500,0) leaves scrollX 0; the only element accepting scrollLeft is the hidden section, at max 167 px. A-7's .flow-table-scroll fix never reached this table (tbl.closest('.flow-table-scroll') is null). J14 NEW-1: .lb-search-name { flex:1; min-width:0 } (styles.css:3009) beside flex-shrink:0 siblings (:3017, :3027) collapses to clientWidth 0 against a scrollWidth of 137-146 px - 'form3/4 EMT coupling' returns 33 rows with no visible names, and nothing overflows, so a scrollWidth === innerWidth check never sees it.
proposal: J14 P1 with the verifier's caveat: below 640 px render each catalog row as a two-line card (name on line 1; part #, price, badge and Add on line 2) using the same display:block grid the manifest already uses; from 641 up give the table a min-width: 640px inside a scroll wrapper - a bare min-width would just be re-clipped by .labor-book-section. NEW-1 folds in: .lb-search-row { flex-wrap: wrap } with the name on its own full-width line below 640. Keep the inline-edit-then-promote behaviour and the 100-row cap, and re-measure the Show-all cost with cards.
event: session_start {vw, vh, coarsePointer} — nobody knows whether a single estimator opens this on a phone

title: "Load into Ledger" is clipped to nothing below ~536 px
item: The Assemblies bar's header is a nowrap flex line whose minimum content is wider than the section it lives in, and that section is overflow:hidden - so on a phone the Load button is laid out past the painted edge and simply does not exist for a finger. The select beside it invites you to pick a saved run recipe, and then nothing happens.
evidence: .assemblies-select { min-width:140px } and .assemblies-load-btn { flex-shrink:0 } inside .assemblies-section { overflow:hidden } (styles.css:1691, :1693, :1646). At 375 px the 148 px button lays out at x 338-486 while the section's painted box ends at x 326; elementFromPoint(346, 441) returns DIV.flow-page. Broken at 390 too. The header needs 436 px of content inside a section that is viewport minus 98, so the real cut-off is about 536 px, not the walker's ~520. Programmatic scrollLeft (max 167) reveals it, so a Magic Keyboard Tab would reach it; no touch gesture will.
proposal: J14 P3, narrowed by the verifier to the two safe options: flex-wrap: wrap on .assemblies-section-header, or move the button into the body next to the select. Do not simply drop overflow: hidden from .assemblies-section - the 436 px header would then spill past the 277 px section and give the flow page horizontal overflow at 375, regressing the zero-overflow property baseline A-6 bought. Rides with T1-09's assembly work and J4 P7's confirm.

title: Conduit and wire children carry numbers the flow won't update or won't show
item: Three defects with one shape: a child row on the bid and the wizard that produced it hold different numbers, and only a Save reconciles them. The overage child is a snapshot of quantity and unit price taken at Save, so changing the run afterwards leaves the waste wrong while the chip still says a live-sounding percentage. The trenching child's manifest quantity and its stored meta diverge, so a correction made on the manifest is silently reverted the next time anyone opens the run. And wire MAC rows have no Price column, yet a book fill writes one and Save persists it, re-hydrating it on every re-entry.
evidence: conduit.js:511-528 and wire.js:140-157 copy ceil(qty x %) and the parent's price once. Parent 150 to 200 ft leaves the child at 15 ft - Conduit $236.50 where $242.00 is right; price 1.10 to 1.25 leaves the child at 1.10 ($272.00 vs $275.00); re-entering shows '200 + 20 = 220' while the bid carries the old line. Trench child edited 150 to 100 on the manifest drops Conduit $750 live, then app.js:171 prefers meta.feet, re-entry reads 150 and Next restores it ($3,964.74 back from $3,214.74) because handleFieldUpdate never touches meta. MAC: an Elliot connector at $206.45 x 6 put Wire at $2,294.71 with $1,056.00 visible in the flow (wire.js:46 has no Price column; laborBookTargets.js:55-61 writes one). All three were downgraded from blocker to stumble because the estimator can edit the child in place and recover - the cost is a wrong figure on the bid meanwhile.
proposal: J5 P4 write-time half only - the verifier killed the read-time variant, because pdf.js, share links, getPurchaseList and getSummaryBreakdown all read the stored child, so deriving at render creates a new stored-versus-shown split. Recompute the overage child when the parent's quantity or price changes in handleFieldUpdate, and treat a manual edit of the child as an override that drops meta.overagePercent (read-only child inputs would add a special row type). J5 P8 lands in the same branch - a trench child's quantity or price edit updates meta.feet/meta.pricePerFoot and regenerates the description - so ship them as one change. J5 P5: give the MAC table the Price column the fittings table has and delete the if (priceNum != null) special case, so the two flows share one rule.

title: Labor on a Permits / Power co. / Temporary power row vanishes from the screen and prints in the PDF
item: Two totals disagree by construction. The summary routes Other-type rows to other charges and adds only their price, so labor typed on a permit row shows no effect at all; the total the PDF prints filters on no type and counts it. So a field takes a number, teaches the estimator that labor does not apply here, and the printed bid then disagrees with the screen by exactly those hours times the rate. A third, unused total disagrees with both.
evidence: getSummaryBreakdown routes OTHER_TYPES to otherCharges and adds only priceAmount (selectors.js:150-152); getTotalLabor filters on no type at all (:18-33); pdf.js:33 calls the second. Permit labor 3 on a qty-1 row: the field keeps 3, the screen's Labor TOTAL (hrs) stays 62.8, getTotalLabor() goes to 65.8, and pdf.js:72 prints 65.8 - a $276.00 screen-versus-print gap at $92/hr. Nothing in code, README or tests says which is intended. J3 NEW-2: getTotalPrice (selectors.js:36-50) is a third total that applies no counts-once rule and also sums Other-charges rows - measured 8,399 against a materialsSubtotal of 7,249 plus $1,150 other - exported but called from no view and no PDF.
proposal: J3 P12: pick a branch - count Other-type labor in the summary, or make the Labor cell read-only with an em dash on those rows - and which branch is J8's call. But the load-bearing clause is the second one: pdf.js:33 must stop calling getTotalLabor() and read the same getSummaryBreakdown().laborTotal the screen shows, or the branch only changes which of the two numbers is wrong. Delete or align getTotalPrice in the same change.
event: pdf_exported {variant, laborTotal, screenLaborTotal} — assert they match

title: A legacy or meta-less book silently loses its defaults, permanently
item: The legacy migration adopts any object as the Labor & Price Book, and the upgrade path then stamps the current defaults version without ever running the merge - so a book that arrives empty or partial is recorded as up to date while missing most of its sections, and never self-heals. Worse, every default missing from a section the book does have is written into the removed map: permanently blacklisted and emitted as a remove correction, so a user proposes deleting defaults they never touched. Separately, every book save stamps a fresh savedAt including the silent boot merge, so a device that boots after an app update can push its stale book over another device's corrections.
evidence: migrateLegacyWorkspace adopts for any object (storage.js:156-158); upgradeLaborBook's bootstrap sets storedVersion = LABOR_BOOK_DEFAULTS_VERSION and the merge is then skipped (state.js:179-190), contradicting that function's own comment. Measured on three shapes: laborBook:{} gives all six tabs at 0 sections with meta {defaultsVersion:2, removed:{}}; absent gives the defaults intact (gear 6/65, conduit 44/373, wire 3/43) as the control; and a partial gear-only book keeps its one row and destroys conduit's 44 and wire's 3 sections (J11 NEW-5). J12 NEW-2: a legacy book with one conduit section booted with 1 conduit section against 44 shipped, and a seed missing five current defaults produced five remove entries in getBookCorrections(). persistBookNow stamps savedAt: new Date() unconditionally (state.js:152-158) from upgradeLaborBook's dirty path (:190). The cloud legacy workspace row takes the same path (cloud.js:92-93).
proposal: J11 P6 in the verifier's preferred variant: run mergeDefaults after bootstrap in upgradeLaborBook and drop the storedVersion assignment - one line, which is also J12 NEW-2's fix. It covers both the empty and the partial shape and self-heals books already in that state, which an 'is it empty?' guard cannot. The savedAt re-stamp needs its own guard: a merge-only save must not move the book newer than the cloud's.

title: `hidden` does not hide — a hole in baseline A-5
item: A-5 fixed elements rendering while marked hidden by shipping two per-class rules and no base rule, so a later class introduced by the N-series inherited the same bug. Four surfaces now render at full size with the hidden attribute set: the Manage Projects create row, the devices flow's assembly-name row, the book's Add-Section row on every catalog tab, and the same class at a fourth site nobody has hit yet.
evidence: .projects-new-row, .inline-name-row { display:flex } (css/styles.css:3667) beats the UA [hidden] rule. Measured with hidden === true: the create row 306x34 px, the assembly-name row 36 px tall with a focusable input, the book's Add-Section row 76 px. A-5 shipped only .header-menu-item[hidden] and .btn[hidden]; laborBook.js:112 carries the same defect unfixed, and projects.js:142 uses the class with no hidden attribute so it is unaffected.
proposal: J4 P4 as reshaped by verifier: one base rule [hidden] { display: none !important } instead of a third per-class rule. It closes device.js:124, projects.js:89-92, laborBook.js:112 and anything the next N-series adds, in fewer lines than the targeted fix, and the class of bug stops recurring.

title: Naming a job ends in a dialog that won't close and a list that grows
item: The very first thing a new user does - naming the job - leaves the Manage Projects dialog open with the typed name still in the field and focus still in it, so Enter again mints a duplicate project and an empty Create mints another 'Untitled project'. Esc is eaten by the field's own keydown handler, so two presses close nothing. On a fresh install, naming the job also leaves the boot project behind, and clicking the header name to rename - the naive reflex - opens the switcher instead.
evidence: Depends on T2-01's CSS. After Enter: row.hidden true, computed display:flex, 34.4 px tall, name still in the input, focus still in the input, '2 projects'. Esc twice from the field does nothing (projects.js:241-244 stopPropagation) while Esc from anywhere else closes. Enter again produced 'Harbor View Clinic TI' twice; empty Create produced 'Untitled project' (state.js:287). The footer '+ New project' toggle flips hidden with no visual change. Rename lives only inside Manage (switcher -> Manage -> Rename -> Enter -> Close = 5 steps).
proposal: J1 P2 = J10 P2, with J10 owning the surface: after Create, clear the field and close the modal when it was opened with {create:true} - the estimator came to name a job, not manage a list - and let Esc close from the field. Plus J1 P3 as narrowed by the verifier: add Rename to the switcher menu and keep the header as the switcher (click-to-edit would split one control into two targets and hide the switcher), and reuse the open project only when it is never-renamed, has no described row and rate 0.

title: Undo is dead exactly when you reach for it, and Redo lies
item: The Undo and Redo buttons are refreshed only at the tail of a full render, and field edits deliberately skip rendering - so after typing, the button is disabled while the stack is not empty, and after an edit clears the redo stack the Redo button stays lit and does nothing. The journey's own trigger is 'relies on Undo when they slip', and the button is dead precisely then. Cold boot is the mirror image: Undo is enabled before the user does anything, and clicking it empties the table.
evidence: updateUndoRedoButtons() is defined at app.js:29 and called from exactly one place, app.js:25 inside render(); it is not exported and no keydown handler binds Z. Typing 99 into a quantity made canUndo() true while #undo-btn.disabled stayed true and Playwright's click timed out; identical after a share-link import and after a spinner click; Add Row wakes it. After an Undo plus one keystroke, canRedo() false with the button enabled and clicking changing nothing. Cold boot: Undo enabled, click gives 0 manifest rows under a hint saying 'type the first fixture below'; reload re-seeds.
proposal: J3 P4's button half, which is the part that adds zero surface: call updateUndoRedoButtons() from handleFieldUpdate, both spinner handlers and updateSummaryOnly. The keyboard half needs a boundary - the browser's own per-field undo already writes through to state via the input listener (measured qty 99 to 9), so an app-level handler firing inside a field runs two undo systems on one keystroke; ship it 'not in a text field' or ship the button half alone. J1 P9: seed the boot row without pushing an undo frame, mirroring what createProject already does at state.js:288-290.

title: Undo frames that undo nothing
item: Several paths push undo frames that produce no visible change, so the first Undo press appears to do nothing and estimators conclude Undo is unreliable. Typing then pausing then blurring re-sends the same value after the coalescing window closed; deleting the last row pushes a second frame for the blank row that replaces it; a no-change flow save deletes and re-creates every child with new ids; and the conduit wizard pushes three frames per pass, so one Undo after a Save removes only the overage.
evidence: manifest.js:398-400 and state.js:411-415. Counted by unwinding the real stack: type 55 into a quantity then Tab immediately = 1 frame, values [55, 40]; type 55, pause 1.5 s, then Tab = 2 frames, [55, 55, 40], and the first Undo leaves 55 on screen. Deleting all six rows then Undo #1 gives 0 top-level rows. A device-flow re-open with flowDirty false then Save: all three child UUIDs changed and Undo left the children at 3 with identical buckets. Conduit undo depth counted non-destructively: no-change re-save 15 to 16; a no-change full pass 16 to 19.
proposal: J3 P5: skip pushUndo when every key in updates already equals the item's coerced value - handleFieldUpdate parses before it calls, so compare after coercion and treat null == null as equal, or a blank price re-sent on blur still pushes a frame - and wrap the last-row re-seed in beginBatch/endBatch. J4 P9: skip the delete-and-re-add when the row set is unchanged, or at least reuse child ids. T1-07 removes the wizard's extra frames for free.

title: The import preview can't show what's about to go wrong, and the type guesser mis-types the trade's own names
item: The preview has no type column, so the estimator cannot see how many rows will arrive needing a type until after the modal closes and they are looking at gold Add buttons. The inference regex misses the commonest lighting names outright - and, worse, mis-types several: a mis-typed row shows a real type badge and sums into the wrong summary bucket with no Add to flag it.
evidence: import.js:13-21 needs fixture/lighting/light fixture; troffer, downlight, exit, emergency, sconce and high-bay all return null, so 2 of 6 real paste lines landed untyped. J2 NEW-1: '2x2 LED Flat Panel - F1' becomes gear (the word panel, import.js:19, because lighting is tested after gear only for fixture|lighting); 'Switchgear MSB', 'Transfer Switch ATS-1' and 'Disconnect Switch 60A' become devices (switch, :17); 'Lighting Contactor LC-1' and 'Fixture Whip' become lighting. On the verifier's seed this put a duplicate Flat Panel row under Gear.
proposal: J2 P4 with the verifier's word-boundary requirement: teach the matcher the trade's fixture names, but fix the order and use word boundaries first - lighting terms must be tested before gear, and switch must not beat switchgear|switchboard|transfer switch|disconnect. The proposed lamp, strip, jack and meter all have false positives waiting (Beam clamp, Strip heater, Jack chain, Voltmeter). J2 P3 as salvaged by the verifier: an info-only chip fails the simplicity budget, so make the dashed 'needs a type' chip a picker (G/L/D/C/W/S) inside the preview - then it replaces the post-import type-modal trip instead of adding surface, and it surfaces the mis-typed rows too.

title: A lower re-count is silently kept, and the preview calls it "no change"
item: The merge is one-directional: it raises a matched row to the import's count when higher and does nothing when lower, while telling the estimator 'already N - no change'. Counts go down as often as up, and 'already 10' reads as reassurance rather than 'your count dropped and I ignored it'. The only way to accept the lower number is to edit the row by hand.
evidence: import.js:88-90 has exactly two branches and no third. Wall Pack 10 in the manifest against an import of 7: preview says 'already 10 - no change' and after Add Overages Only the bid still carries 10 @ $118 / 1.0 h - $354 of material and 3.0 hrs of labor for fixtures the count says are not there. ARCHITECTURE.md:178 documents 'raised when higher' as design, which makes the behaviour intentional but not the wording: the count did change.
proposal: J2 P2 in the verifier's simplest variant: counts are totals and the preview already shows the delta, so 'Update counts' sets matched rows to the import's number in both directions, with 'x 7 - was 10, -3' on screen. Nothing is silent because the delta is visible, and there is no per-line toggle and no new surface - the label change alone is pure removal of a wrong message.

title: "Load into Ledger" replaces all eight sections with no warning and no undo
item: Loading a saved assembly into the devices flow silently replaces every section, including rows the estimator typed a moment earlier - and because the flow is a temp buffer there is no undo path at all. README describes the button as doing something else entirely.
evidence: device.js:367-380. A typed Misc row ('Corridor pull string') was gone after the load with zero dialogs, and the only two dialogs in that run were baseline B-3's discard guard. README:42 still reads 'Load into Ledger - Add assembly items to the manifest' - it loads rows into the flow, replacing what is there, and nothing reaches the manifest until Save and Back.
proposal: J4 P7, with the verifier's note that the README half is pure win and ships regardless. The confirm ('Replace the 5 parts here with "Break room duplex"?') survives spirit rule 1 only because it is gated on there being something to lose. The stronger alternative worth costing: load into the buffer with an 'Undo load' affordance, which puts no decision on the happy path at all.

title: Three doors into the book behave three ways on one row
item: A flow row offers a PB fill button and its own book icon, and they do opposite things: PB replaces the row and closes the book leaving the quantity at 0, while the book icon merges the pick into the row's existing text, producing a Frankenstein description and a summed quantity that nobody could order. An assembly through that door explodes junk rows. A stray click anywhere on a book row that is not an input adds it silently. And the fittings-header door banners a quantity rule it does not follow, with a stale search hiding the group it promised to open.
evidence: laborBookTargets.js:76-82 (merge), :137-165 (explode), :92-100 (fittings door). Measured: the row's book icon produced 'NC POWER SUPPLY&BACK-BOX, CADDY box support far side', qty 2, labor 1.45, book still open; an Assemblies hit through it exploded '20A WIRE TERMINATION x 6 - price 0' plus a labor 0.0075 row. J7 #7: two different non-input areas of a book row (the space right of the trash, the padding of the Name cell) each silently added a child carrying +50 labor hrs, from laborBook.js:495-500. The fittings-header banner read 'x150 on the bid' while Add appended qty 1 with the price as the string "58.4697", and the box still held the previous fill search so the Fittings group was not on screen.
proposal: J4 P6: remove the flow row's book icon and the targetDeviceRow 'Add to' path (laborBookTargets.js:70-86, :141-168; laborBook.js:346-353) and keep PB - 'another part in this section' is + Box then PB, which is what the merge path was standing in for. That deletes ~60 lines, the explode-into-device-rows branch and a banner variant. It must remove only the flow row's icon: the manifest row's book icon is a different, working door that T1-08 depends on. J7 P7: delete the whole-row click handler - 6 lines, and no spec or module depends on it. J5 P9: the fittings-header door clears the fill search and drops the misleading x-footage suffix.

title: The book's search doesn't speak the trade, and its three buckets are three incomplete shapes of one part
item: Everyday electrician phrasings return nothing while the parts sit in the catalog under another name, and the short synonyms that were added to fix that now trade a miss for a screenful of noise because results are ordered by tab and section rather than by match quality. One synonym is matched as a substring, so a four-letter abbreviation inside a longer word ranks a nurse-call power supply first for 'box support'. Structurally the three buckets are incomplete in complementary ways: the catalog has prices and no hours, the curated book has hours and mostly no prices, and the third bucket is named after a vendor.
evidence: 26-query sweep: '2p 20a breaker' returns 0 assemblies while 'encl cb 2p' finds 52; '20a circuit breaker' also 0; 'exit sign' 0/0/0 against 'exit light' 5; '4 square box' returns 17 hits, all 4-11/16; 'emt 90' returns 0 Elliot rows because the catalog writes '90D EMT ELB'; '1900 box', 'single pole switch' and 'pull string' all 0/0/0. 'ss' means stainless in the catalog and set-screw in the book; 'lt' surfaces BATH FAN/LT and a $27,255 generator. In the wire flow 'mac' and 'mac adapter' return 0/0/0 while 'mc connector' returns 2/0/43 and mc-labor-book.json holds 15 'MC CONN' rows. J4 #5: makeTokenMatcher tests synonym alternatives of 4+ chars as substrings, so support -> supp hits SUPPLY and filling from that first Add wrote 1.35 hrs / $45.36 into a row that should read 0.1 hrs. Whole-book counts: 27,556 catalog entries with 0 carrying labor; 481 curated rows with 466 carrying labor and only 98 priced.
proposal: J6 P5 with the verifier's ordering caveat: the load-bearing half is literal-match-first within each bucket, not the synonyms - adding cb -> breaker without it pulls 52 ENCL CB rows into every cb-shaped query and repeats the ss/lt noise this is meant to sink. Then the groups: breaker/brkr/bkr/cb, exit sign/exit light, 4s/4sq/4 square/1900, single pole/1p/sp, 90/90d/ell/elbow/elb, pull string/line/tape, and mac <-> mc (J5 P11 re-shaped smaller by the verifier - a synonym group, not a new defaults section, because the parts already exist). J4 P5: word-boundary matching for synonym alternatives only, verified in-page - (^|[^a-z0-9])supp([^a-z0-9]|$) still matches 'BOX SUPP BRKT' and no longer matches 'SUPPLY', so the abbreviation keeps working; and fill mode ranks Parts before Assemblies. J6 P8 labels the buckets honestly ('Your book (hours)', 'Supply house - Elliot (prices)', 'MC assemblies (hours + material)'), and the last label must not ship until T1-02 lands.

title: Half the book is unreachable and unfilterable
item: The Assemblies side of the book has no filter at all, so narrowing thousands of sections means leaving the tree for the global search and losing your place - even though the input's listeners and its 'N matching sections' count are already written and waiting. Drilling to a common gear item takes four clicks through lower-case MC codes, and the Abbreviation Key that sits two links away decodes none of the codes on the screen behind it.
evidence: #mc-book-search is wired at mcBook.js:183 and :413-416 and appears in neither index.html nor the live DOM; #labor-book-assemblies holds no input or select at all, and its toolbar (index.html:121-124) is exactly the slot the filter would take. Conduit alone has 2,748 sections. The Abbreviation Key modal holds exactly 8 entries (SS, st, cn, insl., RGS, RT, N3R, N4R) and none of D/S, S/S, D/C, S/C, W/C from the book's own rows or nf, gd, hd, seb, n3r from the tree; README:77 calls it a reference for labor codes.
proposal: J6 P6: add the input the code already listens to, styled like the Parts filter - wiring an orphan, not new surface. J6 P10: generate the Abbreviation Key from a table that includes the book's row codes and MC's section codes, add title tooltips on assembly section names ('nf = non-fused'), and fix README:77.

title: Nobody is told the shared book moved, and nobody who contributed learns what happened
item: The loop that turns one shop's know-how into everybody's is closed only in the repository. The merge already computes how many rows it changed and the result is discarded, so nothing anywhere says a user's book was updated. On the contributor's side the row status exists in the table and is readable under RLS, but the 'see what's shared' list never shows it - so an estimator cannot tell whether their correction became everyone's, or whether a number in their book came from a colleague.
evidence: mergeDefaults' return value is dropped at state.js:186, its only call site in the app; after a real v1-to-v2 boot merge the document contains no 'updated', 'shared book', 'merged' or 'changed' anywhere, and neither does the book modal. Provenance badges only ever read You, a supplier name or 'no date' - and the badge is price provenance only (shared.js:76-95), so this journey's own trigger, a labor-hours fix on a price-less row, renders '+ price' and no badge at all.
proposal: J12 P5, blocked on T1-20: the count it would print is inflated by 2 forever until the duplicate name is fixed, and 'changed > 0' is the wrong gate because the merge is not idempotent - gate on a list of actually-changed row names. J12 P4's honest list: the book's rendered trail instead of raw storage keys, the row's status read per row (status is set on all rows in a group, so 'accepted' is readable and 'shipped in v3' is not until B14 adds it), and one line saying the sign-in email travels with it. J12 P3 with the verifier's mechanism correction: the 'shared' cue must live on the row or the hours cell, not on the price badge, which does not exist on a labor-only fix.
event: defaults_merged {from, to, changed} + suggestion_resolved {kind, status, users}

title: Sharing consent is stored per device and survives sign-out
item: The opt-in to share book corrections is a flag in the device's own localStorage, and signing out never clears it - while the post-sign-in sync ends by pushing suggestions, gated only on that flag. So on a shared office machine one person's opt-in silently makes the next person a contributor, pushing their book corrections and their email with no consent of their own. The same device-locality means a second machine shows the toggle Off while the user's rows sit in the table, and cannot withdraw them without flipping it On first.
evidence: isSharing reads localStorage['takeoff-share-corrections'] === '1' (cloud.js:34, :389-395); signOut (:507-514) touches pushTimers, the session, pendingEmail and status but not SHARE_KEY; syncDown ends with pushSuggestions() (:134). The delete on opt-out runs only on a change event (:404-407), so a device whose toggle already reads Off cannot use it. Every pushed row carries email: getEmail() (cloud.js:423), and the modal's 'N corrections shared' line counts the local diff regardless of what the server did (:563-575). Cloud interior is a wall - code-verified, never signed in.
proposal: J12 P4's account-level half, which the verifier promoted out of polish: move the flag into takeoff_store next to book, so two devices agree and consent does not outlive a session on a shared machine. A device-local flag cannot be fixed by copy - this is the only fix. Ships with T2-11's list work.

title: The first sign-in on a new device lands on a blank table and leaves junk on every other device
item: The whole promise of signing in is that the bid shows up. Instead the sync adopts a remote project into the open view only when its id matches the current one, and a fresh device's current project is the empty starter minted at boot with a brand-new id - so the ids can never match and the estimator sees an empty table with a checkmark on it. That starter is then pushed up as a local-only project and appears in every other device's switcher.
evidence: cloud.js:199-206 (the r.id === current.id adopt gate is the only adopt path), :213-219 (local-only push), state.js:212-217 (restoreOnBoot mints a fresh UUID and persists). No auto-switch exists anywhere: syncDown ends at TakeoffApp.render() (:135), and even the legacy-workspace fallback (:226-245) creates a project without opening it. Wall - code-verified, never signed in.
proposal: J11 P7: after syncProjects, when the current project is a description-less starter and remote rows exist, switch to the most recently updated remote project; and never push a starter that has no described row, reusing baseline B-6's meaningful-row test, which identifies it exactly - the starter always carries exactly one description-less row. Step count on the second device drops from 3 to 2 and a class of junk projects disappears rather than needing a cleanup UI. Add the legacy-workspace fallback, which needs the same switch.

title: Deletes don't win
item: Assemblies merge as a union seeded from the remote and overlaid with the local set, so an assembly deleted on one machine returns from whichever machine still holds it. A project deleted on device A does reach the cloud, but nothing tells device B, whose device-local index entry re-uploads it as a local-only project and resurrects the row. 'I deleted that and it came back' is the fastest way to stop trusting sync.
evidence: cloud.js:114-116 (union seeded from remote, then local overlaid), :185-211 (sync only adds and updates index entries), :213-219 (local-only re-upload), :476-482 (onProjectDeleted deletes the cloud row from the deleting device only). Wall - code-verified, never signed in.
proposal: J11 P9: a deleted_at tombstone on takeoff_projects rows and on assembly entries - union, then filter - and syncProjects removes tombstoned ids from the device index. The union at :114-116 and the index-only add/update at :185-219 are exactly the two places it has to be honoured, and onProjectDeleted is the natural place to write one. Invisible to the user; removes the support path with no new UI.

title: Closing the tab in an open flow editor loses the run, with no prompt
item: Every in-app exit from a dirty flow editor asks 'Discard unsaved changes in this editor?', but the browser's own exits do not: the beforeunload handler flushes storage and never sets returnValue. The rest of the app autosaves every keystroke, so the estimator has no reason to expect this page is different - and a Cmd-R, a browser update or a laptop reboot mid-run takes the run silently.
evidence: app.js:378-380 - one beforeunload listener, no returnValue, even with TakeoffState.getFlowDirty() true. Re-driven through the real UI: a typed component row with flowDirty true and storage children 0, then reload = 0 dialogs, lands on the manifest, children still 0; a real tab close behaves identically. The counter-evidence hunt confirms the inconsistency rather than excusing it - the same dirty state exiting in-app does prompt, so B-3 holds and only the browser-level exits skip it.
proposal: J11 P2: set e.returnValue in the existing handler when the flow is dirty and the view is not manifest. Zero decisions on the happy path - flowDirty is false on the manifest and on flow entry, so the guard fires only on a genuinely dirty editor - browser-native copy with nothing to translate, and it removes a rule ('editors are different') rather than adding surface. Must also cover the location.replace in Hard reload, which unloads with no prompt today.

title: Nothing in the app ever says it saved
item: There is no Save control and no saved-state indicator anywhere on the manifest: no timestamp, no 'Saved' flash, not even the word. The only recency surfaces are day-granularity and live inside menus, and the one sentence about persistence is inside the Cloud dialog and talks about devices rather than saving. At the lid-close moment there is no answer to 'is it saved?', so first-timers export a link or print as insurance - extra steps on a route that otherwise costs zero.
evidence: 0 hits for save/saved/saving/autosave across every button, title and aria-label and the manifest view's body text; the project button's only title is 'Switch project'. J11 NEW-1: fmtAgo (views/projects.js:13-22) returns today / yesterday / Nd ago / Nw ago / a date, and grep 'just now' over js/, index.html and css/ finds nothing - so no surface can distinguish 'saved 2 seconds ago' from 'saved this morning'. Scope corrections that strengthen it: the flow editors do carry three Save buttons, and Manage Projects has a second day-granularity 'Updated' column - two recency surfaces, neither saying saved.
proposal: J11 P1 with the verifier's correction: there is no formatter to reuse, so add a minute-level branch to fmtAgo first, then show 'Saved just now / 2 min ago' as the subline or title of #project-switch-btn, appending '- synced 12:47' from lastSyncedAt when signed in. It makes the Cloud button's title and the per-row age say one thing instead of two and adds no control. Must not wrap the header below 900 px.

title: The supplier review queue can never be finished
item: Two and a half thousand uncertain matches are presented as a flat list with no filter, sort, grouping or bulk action, three hundred rows at a time, and every decision re-renders all three hundred. Half of each decision is not even remembered: a Skip only drops the row locally, so the next upload re-derives the identical queue. The rows do not say why they are uncertain, and the button labelled Skip means something entirely different two scroll-heights up the same modal.
evidence: 2,525 rows (847,158 B in mc-elliot-review-queue), 300 rendered, 2,996 DOM nodes, 14,575 px tall, 0 text inputs / 0 filters / 0 sort / 0 bulk actions, 300 selects, footer 'Showing first 300.' Match re-render measured 251 ms in the walk and 1,556 ms in the verify pass. resolveQueueItem(itemNum, null, null) (mcElliotState.js:175-187) leaves mappings at 5 across a Skip and a full second import re-derived the same 2,525. Row 1 shows three candidates all at $0.1334 / 100% with the near-tie at a different price invisible, because the row renders candidates.slice(0, 3) while classifyMatches checked all rivals (elliotPriceCore.js:315-318, :328). Match and Skip give no confirmation: setStatus (mcElliotUpdate.js:288) is wiped by renderBody() (:297 -> :326) and #mc-elliot-status measures empty.
proposal: J13 P3: group by MC category with a filter box reusing TakeoffUtils.makeTokenMatcher, remember Skip as a null mapping so the row stays gone next upload, say why each row is uncertain, and add one bulk action - 'Match all 100% ties with identical prices'. The verifier pinned the rule: it may fire only when all near-tie rivals share the price (elliotPriceCore.js:317), which must be recomputed rather than read off the row's three shown candidates. Rename the row button 'Not this' and keep 'Skip' for categories; set the status after renderBody(), not before.

title: Every line of the supplier tool is written for a developer, and the first one is false
item: The tool's audience is an office admin, and its copy is a developer's: commit, repo, push, overlay, local storage, formula unverified - with no statement of who commits, that a site deploy follows, or that until then only this browser has the prices. The first sentence on the first screen is simply untrue, and the status line goes stale because only one of four handlers ever updates it.
evidence: Verbatim from the run: 'Commit to the repo', 'replace the files in mc-assemblies/', '... and push', 'Add suppliers by editing mc-assemblies/vendor-profiles.json'. The upload panel reads 'No supplier price overlay is active - the book shows original MC prices' while McElliotState.hasOverlay() is false but McBook.elliotImportDate() returns 2026-07-18 and 13 sections of badged supplier parts render behind the modal; after an import it reads '... 177 item prices, 0 new items' for a file with 33,000. Only downloadPatchedBook calls setStatus (mcElliotUpdate.js:317); the overlay, mappings and category-map handlers (:392-411) leave the previous line standing, so after three downloads it still read a category message.
proposal: J13 P4 and P5 together: rewrite the first screen to what is true ('The book's supply-house prices are from the file committed 2026-07-18 (27,556 parts). Nothing has been changed on this computer.'), rename 'Commit to the repo' to 'Send the new prices to everyone' with a paragraph an office admin can act on, keep the file names visible because the maintainer is the reader, and give the three silent download handlers a status line. Retires the word overlay from the UI.

title: Sales tax is a hardcoded 8.5% applied to trenches and backhoes
item: The tax rate is a constant with no input anywhere in the app, so an estimator outside one jurisdiction cannot use the Grand Total at all. And because trenching and rentals are stored as conduit materials, sub-contract and rental dollars are taxed as stock and handed to purchasing as shopping lines nobody can order.
evidence: SALES_TAX_RATE = 0.085 (selectors.js:12); no input on the page matches /tax/. Trenching $1,800 plus a $550 compactor drew $199.75 of one bid's $663.52 tax; on the walk's bid $4,844 of trench, backhoe and sand drew $411.74 of $958.25. The purchase list carries '220 - Trenching: 220 - Dirt @ 24 in - $15.00 - $3300.00' and '4 - BACKHOE - $350.00 - $1400.00' as buy lines (selectors.js:85-94). The sand's labor does land correctly in Conduit labor.
proposal: J8 P7: 'Sales Tax (%)' beside 'Labor Rate ($/Hr)', stored per project like the rate and carried in the share envelope (rides T1-15) - it replaces a constant rather than wrapping it, and removes the 'this app only works in one county' wall. J5 P6 as reshaped by verifier: the walker's version failed the simplicity budget by moving every add-on out of materials, but TRENCHING SAND, ASPHALT PATCH, POLE BASES, CONCRETE PADS and MANHOLES are real stock that belongs taxed and on the PO, and rentals are taxable in many states - so move only the trenching line (a sub-contract) plus add-ons from the Rentals button group, recording the group on the child (the UI already separates Rentals from Fill Materials at conduit.js:170/180). Fill Materials stay materials. Do not add a per-line toggle yet.

title: The bid has nowhere to keep the job's own details, so the form prints another bid's address
item: A project is a name, a manifest and a labor rate - there is no bid metadata at all. The Print-with-Form fields live in a static block of page DOM rather than on the project, so they follow you from one bid to the next and are wiped by a reload. The modal never says which form it is, and the four answers print as a footer after the last item rather than as the header they clearly are.
evidence: storage.js:12 defines the project document. The fields live at index.html:269-274 and are read at print time (app.js:407-415 -> pdf.js:161-167). Filled on bid A, cancelled, switched to bid B and reopened: all three pre-filled with A's values; no localStorage key anywhere contains them; reload empties them. On a 73-row bid the 'Form Details' block lands alone on page 3; on a 44-row bid at PDF y=568 on page 2. No client, GC, due date or bid number exists anywhere in the app.
proposal: J10 P9 and J9 P4 as one change: details {client, address, permitNo, builderOrOccupant, dueDate} on the project document (mirrored in the cloud row's data), edited from the header name, with Print with Form pre-filling from them and printing them under the project name on page 1. It passes the simplicity budget only if #form-modal actually retires - if the sheet ships and the modal stays, it fails. The details must stay optional: nothing here may become a step before typing the first fixture. Needs a sanitize on import and a row in ARCHITECTURE's key table.

title: Print for Purchase Order is not the purchase list
item: The PO PDF is the manifest tree with quantities: it carries price-less grouping rows, the permit, a utility fee and the overage as a separate line, it does not merge duplicates, and it contains no price, no extended cost and no total. Meanwhile the purchase list - which merges, prices, flags what is unpriced and agrees with the summary to the cent - exists on screen and can only be copied. Two 'purchase' artifacts with different contents.
evidence: pdf.js:98-111 prints exactly two x-positions (40 plus indent, and 390). The 44-row file's text runs contain the devices grouping row, the permit, 'Utility service connection fee' and the overage line; zero $ and zero total anywhere. The supply house gets a list with a non-item on it, so the estimator hand-edits it or pastes the TSV into a spreadsheet and prints that.
proposal: J9 P3: reuse getPurchaseList() - Qty, Material, Unit $, Extended $, materials total before tax, project name and date at the top, 'n without a price' flagged - and name the button, the on-screen report and the PDF one thing. Nothing the tree dump prints is lost, because it carries only Item and Quantity with no plan page and no run structure, so the swap has no downside. Keep 'PO' somewhere in the label, because estimators say PO; 'Order list' alone is not trade language.

title: Manifest keyboard & focus
item: One PR over js/views/manifest.js making the table behave the way a spreadsheet does: focus lands where the work is, Tab walks fields rather than buttons, and Enter adds a row.
evidence: activeElement is BODY after the type-modal pick and after Add Row, by click and by Enter, while the ghost 'Add component' row already focuses its new description (manifest.js:446). Tab trace from a row-1 description: x, minus, qty, plus, labor, price, planPage, then the next row's book, arrow and description - 10 stops for 5 fields, 3 Tabs from description to quantity, no tabindex on any of the six row buttons. Both gold 'Add' buttons compute rgb(232,197,71) on rgb(15,15,17) with no title, 69 px apart.
proposal: J1 P7 and J3 P8 with the verifier's accessibility caveat binding: take the row buttons out of the row's inner tab order as a roving-tabindex group or by moving them after planPage, NOT with tabindex=-1, which would remove the book and the delete entirely for a keyboard-only estimator. Prefer a dashed empty 'type...' chip over relabelling the second Add, since it matches what the cell becomes after the pick.
contents: Focus that row's Labor after a type is picked — non-flow types only, since D/C/W already navigate into the editor (J1 F8)
Focus the new description after Add Row, copying manifest.js:442-448 (J1 F8, J3 F8)
Enter in the last field adds a row and moves to it; must not fire while the type modal is open (J3 F8)
Row buttons leave the inner tab order as a roving group, not tabindex=-1 (J3 F8, verifier caveat)
Retire one of the two identical gold Adds — dashed 'type…' chip in the Type column (J1 F7)
Restore the first-run hint and re-hide the zeroed summary when a description is deleted (J1 NEW)

title: One money formatter and one hours formatter, everywhere
item: Four numeric-presentation defects with one cure: the app has several formatters and several precisions for the same figures, so a five-digit total is hard to read, hours disagree with the dollars beside them, the summary and the list round differently, and one price can be a string, a number or a 4-decimal supplier value depending on which door it came through.
evidence: formatMoney is a bare toFixed(2) (manifest.js:112): '$9642.75 / $10462.38 / $11609.88', and every figure on the proof route is five or six digits. Hours print toFixed(1) while dollars use the raw value: 0.75 renders '0.8' beside $63.75, and a total showing 86.3 hrs with $7,935.00 (= 86.25 x 92) when 86.3 x 92 = $7,939.60; the Review PDF rounds per unit so 0.04 and 0.006 both print 0.0. Summary rounds the raw sum while the list rounds per line: $7,807.39 against $7,807.40 with two 4-decimal prices. One search row showed $73.08 and stored the string "73.0758", while an exploded add stored the number 0.23 and a fill stored 1.66; the flows and the manifest inputs render 58.4697 and 206.451 raw, because C-1's decimal rule reached only the review queue.
proposal: J8 P10 owns the touch; J1 P8 and J8 P11 ride inside it (P11 fails the spirit test as a standalone row - nothing is removed and reading correctly is not a step). J1 P4 with the verifier's caveat: use one hours formatter everywhere - the summary, the devices flow's 'Job labor' line and the PDFs - so the same job never prints two totals. Apply C-1's rule (2 places at or above $1, 4 below) to the flow inputs and the manifest Price cell, and settle on one stored type for a price. TSV stays bare.
contents: Thousands separators via toLocaleString in formatMoney and the purchase list; TSV unchanged (J1 F10, J8 F11)
