Hours to two decimals, or '0.75 hrs × $85.00 = $63.75', from one shared formatter (J1 F4, J8 NEW-1, J9 F3)
Round per-line extendeds to cents in getSummaryBreakdown so summary and list share one convention (J8 F10)
C-1's decimal rule reaches the flow inputs and the manifest Price cell (J5 NEW-2, J6 F11)
One stored type for a price — never a string from a search row (J6 F11; the parse itself is T1-10)

title: Trade-language pass — one label map for chip, summary, picker and PDF
item: The screen reads like three applications in one column: shouting all-caps charge types beside title-case categories, software words at the first touch, an internal storage key printed in the PDF's Type column, and one word - assembly - used for three different things at once. One label map, used by the chip, the summary, the picker and the PDF, retires all of it.
evidence: Read off the live DOM: 'SALES TAX (8.5%)', 'Materials TOTAL $', 'Labor TOTAL (hrs)', 'PERMITS', 'POWER CO. CHARGES', 'TEMPORARY POWER' beside Lighting, Gear and Special Systems. 'Assembly Description' is the column header and the placeholder on parents and children, while the devices flow says 'Save as Assembly' and the book has an Assemblies tab. pdf.js:53 prints item.type raw, and J9 NEW-1 measured it truncated to 8 characters: outletsA, trenchin, specialS, powerCoC. MC names arrive verbatim as bid descriptions: '20A ENCL CB 3P (OR 2P' and 'SP              STD'. Casing drift: 'Manage Projects' / 'Manage projects...' / 'New Project' / '+ New project'. The supplier tool's tab reads 'Review Matches (2525)' against a body saying '2,525'.
proposal: J3 P10 with the verifier's addition that the map must reach the PDF, plus J1 P10 and J10 P10. Use 'Fixture or run' for the description column and placeholder, trimmed to 'Fixture or run' on the 204 px phone column; sentence-case the charge types; 'Lines' and 'Last edited' for the projects columns. The verifier trimmed one claim: renaming 'Rows' to 'Lines' does not fix the count, which stays top-level-only - that is B11's job. The PDF half is subsumed by T1-16 and listed here only so the map is built once.

'Assembly Description' → 'Fixture or run' on the column, parents and children; 'Price' → '$ each' (J1 F11, J3 F12)
One TYPE_LABELS map used by chip, summary, picker and the PDF — no raw keys, no 8-char truncation (J3 NEW-1, J9 NEW-1)
Normalise MC names before they become bid descriptions (J6 F16)

Supplier tool tab count matches the body's number format (J13 F10)

title: Import parser hygiene and preview manners
item: One PR over js/import.js and the hash routes, fixing what Count Tooling actually sends and how the preview behaves while it is open. Every item is a removal: a junk row, a silent wrong number, a second normalisation of one concept, a wrong diagnosis, a focus escape.
evidence: The signed-in footer 'View link:<tab><url>' becomes a preview line 'NEW View link: x 0' and then a manifest row with the URL discarded (parseFloat(url) -> 0, import.js:30); the footer's exact shape is pinned in Count Tooling's own tests. '1,800' on the clipboard path becomes 1; '"2,400"' on the link path becomes 0. Three sites use trim().toLowerCase() (import.js:53, :80, :112) while selectors.js:70 also collapses internal whitespace, so 'LED  Wall Pack - WP1' badges NEW and lands as a duplicate even under Add Overages Only. A {v:2} payload reports 'This import link contained no valid items.' Both cold paths leave the blank starter row above the imports with its own Add button. The preview does not trap focus: on the clipboard path Tab leaves for #labor-book-open-btn behind it and Enter re-fires the still-focused paste button.
proposal: J2 P5, P6, P8 and P10's contract text, plus the focus half of J2 P11. The verifier's corrections are binding: normalise at all three import sites plus selectors.js via one shared TakeoffUtils key helper, or the badge and the outcome diverge; guard the blank-row consumption on the sole row being description-less and the import adding at least one row, inside the same batch so Undo restores it. J2 P7's post-import receipt line is explicitly NOT in this batch - the verifier failed it as pure added surface, and its value belongs in T1-04's state-aware button label.

Strip thousands separators; render an unparseable count as '× ?', never 0 or 1 (J2 F6)

title: Book modal chrome & feedback
item: One PR over the laborBook* view modules: make Esc mean the same thing everywhere in the book, say where an add went, prime the search box, give the 100-row cap a way back, and move a maintainer's control off every estimator's lookup screen.
evidence: Esc with focus on an Add button set aria-hidden true while the term 'pull elbow' survived in the input and the module, and reopening showed .labor-book-tabs at display:none over 12 stale rows; Esc from the search box clears then closes, exactly as documented, so the documented behaviour is true one time in three. The only success signal is a 1.2 s check swapped into the button (laborBookSearch.js:178-182), and with no fixture selected a native alert blocks the page. activeElement after the header door is the opener button and after a row icon that row's button; only fill mode focuses the search. A PB fill leaves the fitting row at qty 0. 'Show all 3,937 parts' replaces the body with every row (laborBookElliot.js:54-62, :236-239) and nothing re-renders the capped body while data-loaded=1 stands. Signed out the footer reads 'Export Groups & Sections - Close' with the admin button already hidden two positions away.

The verifier's notes: P4 removes a special case rather than adding one, since both handlers already exist (laborBook.js:653-656 and app.js:91-102); priming focus must keep P4's Esc contract intact; and the selectors half of the qty-0 fill is T1-05's, so this batch only seeds the row at 1.

title: The part card and the provenance trail
item: The provenance system is a differentiator whose promise is 'every number has a trail'. Ten defects break that promise at its edges: the commonest way of entering a price leaves no trail at all, clearing a price leaves a fresh green badge on an empty field, a promoted part inverts the rule the rest of the journey teaches, the history is not in date order, and the card cannot be scrolled on a laptop.
evidence: laborBookCard.js:32-36 mints a synthetic 'You' offer that the first real quote replaces outright, and updateLaborBookRow writes no history - after recording Border States $3,980 nothing remembers the $4,025 typed first. A cleared price leaves {price:'', priceSource:'You', pricedAt:today, edited:true} and the badge still reads 'You - today' in the in-place patch and after a full render, because shared.js:78 needs no source AND no date to show the ghost. J7 NEW-2: on a promoted catalog part the import offer already fills offers[0], so offers.length === 1 is false and recording Crescent $221.40 left the row at Elliot $259. J7 NEW-3: history renders in insertion order while every line shows a date. J7 NEW-4: recordPartPrice writes the typed casing into row.priceSource, so a badge reads 'summit electric' while the table reads 'Summit Electric'. At 1440x768 the card is 691 px holding 794 px behind .part-card-content{overflow:hidden} (styles.css:3383) and scrollTop stays 0; injecting overflow:auto fixed it in the page. Empty supplier plus a price does nothing, with zero error nodes; an emptied date silently records today (state.js:599). The offers table has 0 editable cells while ARCHITECTURE.md:109 still promises a badge popover.
proposal: J7 P6, P8, P2 and P12's doc half. Verifier corrections: the .pc-body max-height clause of P8 is unnecessary because History already has its own working scrollport, and the empty-date tier needs recordPartPrice to stop defaulting at, not just card copy; P2 is narrower than written - open sections already survive, so the whole fix is openSections.add for the new section plus restoring focus to the field just edited. Do not rename the 'In use' pill; add the sentence instead (that half is G7).
contents: Inline price edits push a real 'You' offer and a history line; drop the synthetic branch (J7 F5)
Clearing a price clears priceSource/pricedAt and returns the '+ price' ghost (J7 F6)

History in date order (J7 NEW-3); canonical supplier casing on the row badge (J7 NEW-4)

Promotion keeps your place: openSections.add for the new section, restore focus (J7 F2)

title: The devices flow's shape
item: The flow opens as a wall of eight identical empty tables with a title pointing at the wrong one, a panel figure that counts nothing orderable, and an assembly card padded with blank lines. Collapsing what is empty is the single biggest scroll saving anywhere in the app.
evidence: Measured empty: 1183 px tall in two columns at 1440 (section lefts 125 and 740) and 1925 px in one column at 1199 - 1.6x, not the walker's 'double'. Five of eight sections stayed empty on the walked journey. Title 'Devices - Add Boxes and Covers' over a first table headed 'Outlets and Switches'. The panel's Quantity read 60 - receptacles plus boxes plus covers added together. '+ Box' leaves activeElement on body. saveAssemblyAs keeps blank seed rows (device.js:293-299, no isMeaningfulRow filter) so the card listed three real rows and five '- x 1 | Labor: 0 | Price:' lines, and device.js:299 manufactures a blank row for a section that had none. flowDirty is true before and after Save as Assembly - design-correct, but the word Save means two scopes on one page.
proposal: J4 P8 and P9, with J4 P10's labelling half. The verifier measured the win (a header plus one chip row replaces 1183 px at 1440 and 1925 px at 1199) and confirmed the chips keep all eight section names discoverable, so nothing is hidden, only deferred. Ordering note: '+ Box focuses the new description' is unreachable until T1-01 lands, because today the click on + Box right after typing is swallowed and the row is never added at all.
contents: Render a section's table only when it holds a meaningful row; otherwise one row of '+ Outlet/Switch', '+ Box'… chips (J4 F8)
Title the page with the run's own name (J4 F8)
Drop the panel's summed 'Quantity' — a count of nothing orderable (J4 F9)
'+ Box' focuses the new description — blocked on T1-01 (J4 F9)
Filter isMeaningfulRow in saveAssemblyAs; stop manufacturing a blank row per empty section (J4 F11)
Drop the name row's Cancel so one page stops carrying two Cancels with different scopes (J4 F11)
Label the two saves distinctly (J4 F12)

title: Conduit and wire step labels
item: The wizard uses one vocabulary for two kinds of thing, repeats one number three ways without a unit, and gives its percentage buttons no pressed state. The table split is not only a labelling fix - recording which button group a row came from is the data T2-19's reshaped tax fix depends on.
evidence: The add-on table heads verbatim 'Description - Quantity (Hours or Days) - Additional Labor - Charge (per Hour or Day)' over one table (conduit.js:191) that receives TRENCHING SAND and BACKHOE alike, while the two button groups above it already know the difference (:170 Rentals, :180 Fill Materials); 'Additional Labor' has no unit at all. The parent panel says 'Quantity: 150' and 'Length: 150' on step 1 and 'Current length: 200' on step 3, with no 'ft' anywhere. All four percentage buttons compute class="" after a click (shared.js:41-46 renders no state). The preset select appends below the blank seed row and resets itself (conduit.js:414-424), leaving one trash click per run; FITTINGS_LIST is six bare strings.
proposal: J5 P9. The verifier's notes: 'carries the preset's labor when present' is a data task first and ships nothing until fittings.js grows fields, so it is not in this batch; and the Rentals / Fill split is what the reshaped J5 P6 needs, so record the button group on the add-on child here. Baseline C-7 was explicitly delegated to J5 by the baseline, so the preset-select item is not a re-report.
contents: Split the add-on table into Rentals (Hours/Days · Rate) and Fill & site (Qty · Unit price), recording the group on the child (J5 F10)
The preset select fills the blank seed row when one is empty (J5 F11, baseline C-7)
One parent-panel line carrying the unit — '220 ft' (J5 F12)
An .active class on the chosen % button (J5 F12)

title: Summary and purchase-list display rules
item: Three display rules that let a wrong-looking number stand: a minus sign is treated three different ways with no visual cue, a zero price and a missing price look alike but count differently, and the purchase list gives the quantity column exactly as much room as the description.
evidence: min="0" is on the inputs and :invalid matches, but grep ':invalid' css/styles.css returns 0 rules and the computed border colour equals a valid neighbour's. Price -28 x 20: summary Special $0.00 (the p > 0 guard) while the list honours $-28.00 / $-560.00, a $560 disagreement; labor -0.4 x 10 subtracts 4.0 hrs with no guard at all; qty -10 falls into the counts-once branch and adds $38.00 while the list drops the row; a labor rate of -92 turned a $17,024.67 bid into $1,154.67. Price 0 renders '$0.00 - dash' and is not counted as unpriced, while blank renders 'dash - dash' and is - manifest.js:282's l.extended ? ... : '-'. The purchase list is table-layout: fixed, so at 375 px all four columns are 82 px with descriptions wrapping to five lines, and at 768 px all four are 180 px.
proposal: J8 P3 with the verifier's caveat that it must be clamp OR credit, not both - the 'alternatively' is a second proposal - and clamp is the branch that also covers negative labor and negative quantity; J3 P7's clamp half agrees, and must fire on change or blur rather than input, or a user typing a minus before the digits loses the keystroke. J8 P9 minus its optional '(no charge)' text, which the verifier identified as the only additive part. J14 P9's purchase-list third, which the verifier confirmed helps at 768 as well.
contents: Clamp price, labor, quantity and the labor rate to ≥ 0 on change, with a visible invalid state (J8 F3, J3 F6)
A $0 price renders $0.00 · $0.00 and is never 'without a price'; blank stays dashed and counted (J8 F9)
Purchase list table-layout: auto with Qty / Unit $ / Extended $ at width:1% (J14 F11)

title: Export and share surface
item: One PR over the share and export paths: tell a recipient what they are holding, stop making identical twins, fail loudly on a shaped-but-empty link, name the files after the job, and move the share verb to where the estimator is standing at delivery time.
evidence: No text matching /copy/ anywhere on the recipient's page; exportedAt is decoded and ignored (app.js:447 stamps new Date()); the '(shared Sep 6)' suffix is cut by the switcher at both 1440 px (scrollWidth 297 vs clientWidth 237) and 375 px. app.js:448 always calls createProject with no lookup by name or exportedAt, so one link opened twice gives two byte-identical projects - and duplicating a bid twice does the same for '(copy)'. {"v":2,"name":"x"} and a non-array manifest both strip the hash and do nothing, while garbage and a 300-char cut do alert. suggestedFilename is identical for a 3-row and a 44-row bid: takeoff-review.pdf, takeoff-purchase-order.pdf, takeoff-form.pdf (pdf.js:74, :115, :169). The blank app shows no print, share or export word anywhere, and ☰ holds exactly New Project, Export via link, Remove items and Hard reload.
proposal: J9 P5 minus the confirm prompt, which the verifier failed: it adds a decision to a path measured at 1 step and 0 decisions, and removes nothing, because the switch replaces nothing - both the recipient's own starter and the sender's bid were intact after import. The banner, the name-plus-exportedAt dedupe and the shaped-but-empty alert pass all four tests on their own. J9 P6 (filenames; skip the 'Saved' flash, which duplicates the browser's download chip; slug must strip / and :). J9 P7 as a MOVE, not an addition - the verifier rejected keeping both surfaces by construction. J10 P5's ' 2' suffix must cover Duplicate as well as #d=.
contents: A dismissible 'Copy of X, shared Sep 6 by link — edits stay on this device' banner on #d= import (J9 F7)
Dedupe by name + exportedAt instead of creating a second identical project; same ' 2' suffix for Duplicate (J9 F6, J10 F15)
Alert on a shaped-but-empty payload — a missing or non-array manifest is as silent as garbage is loud (J9 F9)
Project-and-date filenames for all three PDFs (J9 F8)
'Copy share link' moves under Print Options and the ☰ item is removed (J9 F10)

title: The projects surface
item: One PR over js/views/projects.js and its CSS: stop the list re-sorting under the estimator, make long names distinguishable, let the menu scroll, put the delete confirm in the row with the facts in it, and make the Rows column count what it claims.
evidence: getProjects sorts by updatedAt (state.js:245) and applyRename stamps savedAt (projects.js:188-194), so renaming a non-open bid jumps it to row 1 while the open bid sat at index 13 of 24 - and leaving a bid stamps it too, so the open bid is never pinned. The header name shows 237 px of 519-536 px with the button's only title reading 'Switch project' and the name span carrying none; menu names clip at 250 px, also untitled, so three Northgate variants at 63/70/78 chars render as one identical line. The menu has max-height: none and overflow: hidden: at 24 bids it is 919 px against a 900 px window with the footer at y 922, reachable only because the header is position: static. The open bid's row offers only Rename and Duplicate, neither with a title, and Delete is a native confirm naming the bid but not its row count. The Rows column counts top-level entries of the stored manifest: 1 for a fresh bid, 8 for an 11-line bid, and 5 while memory held 6 inside the 400 ms debounce.
proposal: J10 P4, P5, P6, P8 and P10's count half. Verifier notes: pinning the open bid is the half that actually removes the second look, since the stamp also fires on leaving; hover is desktop-only so the middle-ellipsis half is what carries the phone; the archive idea raised in F8 is a separate proposal (X9) and not part of P6; the inline Delete's row count inherits F6's under-count until the count itself is fixed, so ship both together.
contents: Pin the open bid; stop stamping updatedAt on rename (J10 F5)
Full-name title on the header button and every menu row; middle ellipsis so the suffix survives; '(copy)' and '(shared …)' as chips (J10 F7)
The menu scrolls with its footer outside the scroll; sticky footer in the modal (J10 F8)
Inline delete confirm carrying the row count; a disabled Delete with a reason on the open bid (J10 F10)
The Rows column counts what it claims, not top-level only (J10 F6)

title: The phone batch — coarse pointer and ≤640 px
item: Everything below 640 px that is cramped rather than unreachable (the unreachable ones are T1-22 and T1-23). Order matters inside this batch: the card grid must be fixed before the font size is raised, or the quantity clipping gets worse before it gets better.
evidence: Card grid tracks at 375 px measure 24.02 / 104 / 38.95 / 38.95 / 46.73: the quantity box is 44.8 px with 27 px of content space, so '4500' (32 px of glyphs) renders '450' and '12000' (40 px) is worse; Labor and Price keep width:4.25rem = 68 px inside 39 px tracks, overflowing 29 px each with Price overlapping the Plan track by 18 px. 151 of 151 manifest controls fail 44x44, 70 in both dimensions, and the qty plus has no halo - a centred tap ran 24 to 25 while +/-14 px hit-tested DIV.qty-spinner or the TR and did nothing. 74 of 74 inputs are under 16 px (14.4 manifest, 13.333 flow, 13.6 card) and 64 type=number inputs carry 0 inputmode. The import preview's content is 500 px at x -62 to 438 with the title reading 'ort Preview' and Add All 38 px off the edge with 42 px tappable; nothing scrolls because a fixed .modal adds no document scroll width, and a real tap at x 371 did complete the import. The devices flow is 2,356 px against an 812 px viewport with Save at document y 2,255 and zero fixed-or-sticky elements. The switcher menu runs x 117 to 455 on a 375 px screen and takes window.innerWidth and document.scrollWidth to 455 until it closes.
proposal: J14 P4, P5, P6, P2, P8 and the two thirds of P9 that survive, plus J10 P7. Binding verifier caveats: P4's arithmetic does not close as written, because the two 24 px spinner buttons live in the qty track - it must grow past 6.5 rem or the spinners must leave it; P6 must ship with or after P4; P5 should reuse .labor-book-add-btn's existing 44 px idiom rather than inventing a second one; P2's min-width: min(500px, 94vw) still beats the computed max-width, so raise the max-width alongside it, and dropping the 'In Manifest' column loses the only place a manifest row absent from the import is visible; and P9's .project-menu { right: 0 } is WRONG - it anchors to the button's right edge at x 264 and would drop a 338 px menu off the left instead, while max-width: calc(100vw - 1.5rem) does not clamp it. Anchor to the header's left edge or clamp the width.
contents: Card grid phone shape so a four- or five-digit quantity is readable and Labor/Price/Plan stop fusing (J14 F4)
16 px inputs under (pointer: coarse) and inputmode='decimal' on all 64 number inputs — after the grid fix (J14 F6)
Coarse-pointer control sizes with real hit areas, reusing the existing 44 px idiom; 'PB' → 'Book' (J14 F5)
Import preview fits the phone: min-width and max-width raised together, one column below 640 (J14 F2)
A sticky Save bar in the flows below 640 (J14 F8)
Manage Projects rows stack below 640 (J14 F9, J10 F9)
The switcher menu stops widening the layout viewport — anchor left or clamp the width (J14 F10, J10 F9)

title: Cloud, sign-in and status honesty
item: One PR over js/cloud.js and the unload handler: make both sign-in buttons behave the same way and stop showing a stale message, say what kind of account this is, stop dressing a safe recovery control in red, stop the checkmark claiming a push that has not happened, and label Sync Now for what it actually does.
evidence: Empty Sign In returns silently (cloud.js:663-666) with zero network requests while the code button says 'Enter your email first.'; msgEl is never cleared on the silent return, so that message sits under an unrelated Sign In click (J11 NEW-3). The modal says the emailed code creates an account, ARCHITECTURE.md says accounts are provisioned, README says nothing, and the signed-in body carries no account-kind hint. Hard reload is class header-menu-item-danger, computed rgb(232,84,71), with '(keeps your data)' only in a hover title - and caches.keys() is empty with 0 service workers, so it clears nothing. setStatus('syncing') appears only at cloud.js:78; signOut (:507-514) clears pushTimers without pushing, dropping queued book and assembly writes as well as project ones; beforeunload never calls flushPending, visibilitychange is the only flush, and there is no keepalive anywhere (J11 NEW-4). Sync Now pushes at :106-108, :207-210 and :213-219, so the 'pull, not push' claim was half-killed. J11 NEW-2: after the legacy migration the index entry carries the legacy savedAt (storage.js:159), so the project you are looking at reads 'Jul 14'. J12 #7: the sharing list prints storage keys and renders price-less values as '8 hrs - $—'.
proposal: J11 P3, P4 and the honest half of P13/P14, plus J12 P4's wording items and P9's README line. Verifier notes: P3's scope widens to clearing msgEl on every entry to signIn and send; P4's rename must land WITH the service worker (X2) if that ships, since only then does Hard reload have a cache to clear; P10's Sync Now sentence must read 'reconciles this computer with the cloud - the newer copy wins each way'.
contents: One behaviour for both sign-in buttons; clear msgEl on every entry (J11 F4, J11 NEW-3)
Say what kind of account this is after a code-created first sign-in (J11 F5)
'Reload app (keeps your data)' — drop the danger styling (J11 F6)
The status stops claiming a push that is still queued; signOut flushes; beforeunload calls flushPending (J11 F13, J11 NEW-4)
Label Sync Now as a two-way reconcile; surface the ⚠ Cloud error outside the modal (J11 F14)
The post-migration index date stops reading as the legacy date (J11 NEW-2)
The sharing list uses the book's rendered trail, not storage keys, and drops '$—' (J12 F7)
Say that the sign-in email accompanies every correction (J12 F9)

title: Merge hygiene and admin guards
item: One PR over the merge module and the two admin panels: let provenance flags heal so a user stops proposing corrections they did not make, put guards on the review panel so a fat-fingered number or a chimera group cannot ship, stop provenance dates resetting on every re-import, and stop shipping internal flags into repo artifacts.
evidence: Trashing 'wire · THHN CU · 12' then adding it back at the exact default still yields 'remove 12' and no 'new', because computeCorrections' guard (laborBookMerge.js:144) only drops names that left the defaults, never names whose row is present; renaming '14' to '14 SOL' and back leaves 'remove 14' with the row sitting there. updateLaborBookRow sets edited (state.js:569) and nothing clears it: 10.8 to 11.3 to 10.8 leaves the flag, and when upstream moves that row to 11.2 the row stays at 10.8 and the diff flips to proposing 11.2 -> 10.8. suggestionsReview.js:38-39 takes medLabor and medPrice from independent median() calls; the outlier test at :43-44 requires kind === 'edit' and a price, so 8 -> 800 hrs and a brand-new part at 800 hrs are both unflagged; downloadAcceptedPatch (:146-174) re-emits every accepted row ever with no shipped marker. partNumber never leaves the machine, verified by dumping a correction's keys. stampNewItemDates passes only McElliotState.getOverlay() (mcElliotUpdate.js:153), so a part unchanged since 2026-07-18 came back stamped today and meta.elliot.importedAt moved with it. The downloaded overlay carries newItemsTruncated and allCats at 3,663 B against 1,920,728 B committed. index.html:165 is type="text" and no updateUser or resetPasswordForEmail exists in js/ or the Edge Function.
proposal: J12 P2 and P6, J13's provenance-date and artifact items, and the Manage Users password item. Verifier notes that bind: P2's removed-splice must fire on both the rename-back and the Add-Row-back paths, and 'equals the shipped default' is undefined while a section carries two rows of one name, so T1-20 lands first; P6 must also cover the kind:'new' rows the outlier test skips entirely, and partNumber must join the payload or an accepted new part reaches the maintainer with nothing to key the catalog on.
contents: Splice a name out of laborBookMeta.removed when the row comes back — both rename-back and Add-Row-back (J12 F2)
Clear `edited` when a row equals the shipped default again — blocked on T1-20 (J12 F3)
Labor outlier guard, and one that also covers kind:'new' rows (J12 F8)
Reject groups whose labor and price medians come from different users unless ≥ 3 users (J12 F8)
A `shipped` status so the next patch is a delta, not a re-apply (J12 F8)
partNumber travels with a `new` correction (J12 NEW-3)
Provenance dates stop resetting on re-import; meta.elliot.importedAt stops moving for unchanged parts (J13 F9)
Internal flags out of the downloaded artifacts; a size sanity check on every download (J13 F11)
Manage Users: the temporary password stops being type="text", and the missing reset path is named (J13 F13)

title: Your first bid in five minutes
item: Takeoff Tooling has no guides at all — README.md is the only user-facing document — so Tier 4 is a guide-writing backlog, not a list of edits. This first article is the make-or-break ten minutes: type a fixture, give it a type, price it, set the rate, read the total.
evidence: J1's demo moment measured at about eight seconds from an empty app to $89.50 · $7.61 tax · $97.11, on a phone as well as a desktop. README says 'Quantity … default 0', which is wrong for a described row, and documents neither projects nor the labor rate nor the first-run hint.
proposal: Carry: 'Add' in the Type column sets the type (or press L/G/D/C/W/S); Labor is hours per unit; the labor rate lives in the totals panel; autosave is automatic and there is no Save button; a project is a bid, and where to rename or delete one. Until T1-05: a row at quantity 0 with a price still counts once — take a row off the bid by removing it, not by typing 0. Until T1-01: Tab from Plan Page reaches the labor rate in two presses and sidesteps the swallowed click.

title: From count to bid (and the #import= contract)
item: The hand-off article, plus the only place the link format is written down for the people on the other side of it.
evidence: README:58-59 describes both import buttons inaccurately; ARCHITECTURE.md:179 has the payload shape and README has nothing. The verifier confirmed `type` is compared case-sensitively against ITEM_TYPES (import.js:212) and that a wrong `v` is reported as an empty link.
proposal: Walk the paste and the link with the preview's deltas. Say what each button really does. Rows the import could not type show a gold Add. Name what arrives from Count Tooling: fixture-tab-count-tab-pages, 'ft of …' rows becoming Conduit and Wire, the 'View link:' footer. Publish the contract: pin v:1 literally; description; count or quantity; page or planPage; type as one of exactly lighting, gear, devices, conduit, wire, specialSystems, permits, powerCoCharges, temporaryPower; and that a 'px of' row means a page was left unscaled upstream.

title: Shaping the bid
item: Types, components, remove, and what undo actually covers — the article that stops the three wrong turns the naive walk took.
evidence: TakeoffState.removeItem has exactly one caller app-wide; the × beside a chip is the only control shaped like remove and it removes the type, moving the row's dollars to Misc. Coalescing (1.2 s), the 50-frame cap and the button-refresh rule are documented nowhere.
proposal: Carry: Add then pick, or G L D C W S; Devices/Conduit/Wire open their editor at once and the chip reopens it; × clears the type and parks the money in Misc until re-typed; the ↳ rail, the 'Add component' ghost row, components having no plan page, and one Undo restoring a deleted parent with all its children. Undo/redo is manifest-only, one step per typing burst, 50 deep, and leaves the editor. Do not delete a row by zeroing its quantity. Finding J3 #1 must never appear in a guide — it has to be fixed (T1-14), not documented.

title: Parts under a device run
item: The article that has to carry the app's most dangerous undeclared rule until T1-08 changes the default.
evidence: The quantity semantics are stated nowhere in README, CLAUDE.md or ARCHITECTURE.md, and the two doors onto one row disagree in silence. README:42's Load-into-Ledger line is wrong.
proposal: Carry: the chip with the pencil is the door (or press D in the type modal and you are already there); quantities are totals for the whole line, not per run — until T1-08; PB fills the row from the book; the panel's Price is what lands in the Devices bucket; two saves on one page, and do both; Load into Ledger replaces what is in the flow. Until T1-01: a field is not committed until you leave it, and the first click after typing may not register — otherwise the article teaches a route that silently drops numbers.

title: Trench, fittings and waste on a conduit run
item: The wizard's commit rule is a design fact developers know and estimators do not, and until T1-07 lands it is the single most expensive thing an unwarned user can hit.
evidence: README:45-51 is two sentences and does not say that Next writes to the bid, that Back does not undo, what an overage costs, or that MAC adapters have no price column. CLAUDE.md and the baseline record the commit rule for developers.
proposal: Carry: quick-add sets material, depth, price per foot and the footage; rentals are hours-or-days times rate; Next saves that step onto the bid and Back does not undo it, with Undo working once per step — until T1-07; fittings, where PB fills a row and the preset list only fills a name; overage is ceil(ft × %) at the run's own price with no labor and is frozen at Save, so re-open and Save after changing the footage — until T1-24; MAC adapters take a price only through PB and do not show it — until T1-24; search 'mc connector', not 'mac adapter' — until T2-09.

title: Finding a part
item: How to read three buckets that are three incomplete shapes of one part, and the only decoder for the MC tree until T2-10 ships one.
evidence: Measured across the whole book: 27,556 catalog entries with 0 carrying labor and 27,544 priced; 481 curated rows with 466 carrying labor and 98 priced. README:73 and ARCHITECTURE:186 describe a rolled-up-or-exploded choice that does not exist.
proposal: Carry: pick the fixture first, or open the book from the row's icon, then type the trade name; read the three lists as hours / prices / both, saying plainly that a supply-house row brings no hours and a book row may bring no price. What Add does: one child under the fixture at the fixture's count — for a run, set the count yourself, until T1-03 — and an assembly adds its components as separate lines and may price them differently, so check the BOM footer, until T1-02. The tree: Equipment → Switchs/Breakers → encl cb = enclosed circuit breaker; nf/f = non-fused/fused; n1/n3r/n4x = enclosure ratings. 'MC assemblies (hours + material)' must not be written as a bucket label until T1-02 lands, or it promises a number the add does not deliver.

title: Recording a quote
item: The provenance system is a differentiator that nothing user-facing explains: not quotes, not 'In use', not the card, not promotion, and not the snapshot rule that decides whether a bid follows a price change.
evidence: README:72 describes the badge only; ARCHITECTURE.md describes the book side and is stale on the popover. The snapshot rule — a child keeps the price it was added with — is stated nowhere, and the verifier confirmed a child carries no link back (meta null).
proposal: Carry: book icon → find the row → click the price pill, which is the door → supplier, price, date → Record. The three pill colours by age, with the boundaries as verified (<30d fresh, 30–90d aging, >90d stale). 'In use' means the price this book row carries; parts already on a bid keep the price they were added with. Editing a supplier part copies it into your book under the same section name, and the supplier's price stays as their offer. Until T1-10: type prices without a dollar sign or commas.

title: Check the bid before it goes out
item: Where every number comes from — and the home the verifier chose for J8 P6 after failing it as a UI addition, because the flow's own line stays and nothing would be removed.
evidence: README documents none of this: no summary, no labor rate, no sales tax, no purchase list. The summary carries zero title attributes and no drill-down; the only explanation of parent-plus-component labor is inside the devices flow.
proposal: Carry: how each bucket is built, with the parent-3.6-plus-components-6.0-equals-9.6 example; what the purchase list includes and excludes and why its total is before tax; what 'n without a price' means. Until T1-05: a priced row at quantity 0 still counts once and is absent from the list. Until T2-19: tax is fixed at 8.5% and applies to trenching and rentals. Until T1-13: what ≠ means, and that overage lines must be added to the run's footage by hand on the order. Until T1-12: do not edit a quantity while the list is open.

title: Deliver the bid
item: What each print contains, and the one sentence that stops two people reading two different totals off the same link.
evidence: README's Export section is four accurate but shallow bullets; none describes what any PDF contains. The link is 318 chars per row (about 95 kB for a 300-row bid), the fragment never reaches the server, and a cut link alerts while a link mangled into valid JSON without a manifest does not.
proposal: Carry: where Print Options is; what each print contains; the form's purpose and fields; Copy purchase list then paste into a spreadsheet. Sending someone the bid: it carries the whole bid, the recipient needs no account, they get a copy and edits do not flow back — and until T1-15, tell the recipient the labor rate. The link is the bid: it works offline and stores nothing on a server, a chat client that cuts long links produces the 'truncated' message, and if nothing opens at all, ask for the link again.

title: Running several bids
item: The five verbs of a week with three live bids, plus the two warnings that keep an estimator out of T1-17's blast radius while it is queued.
evidence: README has no Projects section at all, although this file's own coverage matrix assumes one.
proposal: Carry: create, switch, rename via Manage, duplicate as a template, delete (open another bid first); '(copy)' is your template and '(shared <date>)' is a colleague's, so rename it. Until T1-17: save or cancel the editor before switching bids, and if you do land on the blank screen, do not switch to a copy of the same bid — go back to the one you were editing. Until T1-15: check the labor rate on every new or shared bid. The Rows number counts lines, not components.

title: Saving, signing in, and two computers
item: Lead with the fact nothing in the app states: there is no Save button because it saves as you type, in this browser. Then what signing in is actually for.
evidence: Zero save-words anywhere in the manifest view. README's Cloud Sync paragraph is stale ('Newest save wins for the workspace' — there is no workspace), and the verifier disproved the walker's own 'Sync Now pulls, it doesn't push'.
proposal: Carry: no Save button; what is not autosaved (an open flow editor until you press Save); sign-in is optional and is for a second computer; password versus emailed code, and that a code-created account will always use the code. What syncs (takeoffs individually, your book, saved assemblies) and what does not (which takeoff is open, supplier-price overlays). One line each: newer save wins per takeoff, the book follows the newest edit, assemblies add up. Sync Now reconciles both ways — the newer copy wins each way. Offline works until you refresh; do not refresh without signal. Until T1-21: reload before you start editing on a second machine.

title: Fix a number once, fix it for everyone — plus the two admin articles
item: The shared book's own article, and the two admin ones: loading a supply house's price file, and letting a new estimator in. Roles and Manage Users are undocumented anywhere today.
evidence: 'shared book' occurs exactly once in the whole app, inside the signed-in branch of the cloud modal; README:84 is the only user-facing mention and it is silent on the email. README:76 is the only line about the supplier tool. Both admin flows contain steps (a git commit, a Pages deploy, an out-of-band password hand-off) that no screen explains.
proposal: Article one: where the toggle is, what a correction is, what leaves the machine (book rows and your sign-in email; never a takeoff), how to withdraw, and that accepted fixes arrive in an app update and never override a row you changed yourself. Article two, 'Loading the supply house's price file': who has the button, where it hides, what the summary numbers mean in trade terms, what 'Skip' means in each of its two places, and the hand-off — four files, the site maintainer, everyone's book updating on reload; include the recovery line until T1-18, and say that Remove overlay also clears the review queue. Article three, 'Letting a new estimator in': the emailed-code path is self-serve, Manage Users is for roles, and roles take effect only after the person signs in again.

title: Takeoff Tooling on an iPad or phone
item: The device article — and the one place the synthesis had to overrule the dossier, because the workaround it recommends does not work.
evidence: README, CLAUDE.md and ARCHITECTURE.md say nothing about tablets, phones, touch or breakpoints; the four breakpoints are documented only in CSS comments. J14 NEW-1 proved the book's global search shows no part names at all at 375 px, which is exactly what the dossier's guide action told phone users to rely on.
proposal: Carry: portrait is cards and landscape is the office table, with the flip at 900 px; flow tables slide sideways, so swipe a row to reach Price and the trash; Save lives at the bottom of a flow; tap the provenance pill for the part card and Record price at the counter. Until B12: pinch out after typing on an iPhone. Until T1-04's preview fix: pasting from Count Tooling works on the phone even though the preview is cut off — the visible sliver of Add All does fire. The line 'on a phone use search, not the supplier sections' must NOT be written until T1-22 lands.

title: Nothing refreshes a bid row from the book when a quote changes
item: The strongest gap, and it is J7's actual trigger: build the bid, then quote it, and every changed price needs the child deleted and re-added by hand. Bid rows are snapshots by design, which is correct behaviour with the wrong words and no hint.
evidence: A child '75KVA Transformers.3PH' stayed $3,950 / 32 hrs after the book row moved to Border States $3,925 / 35.5 hrs, and the child carries no link back (meta null). The storage already exists: every manifest item carries a meta field, sanitized on import (state.js:68), cloned on export (:390) and seeded null on create (:289), and only the conduit flow writes it today — so meta.book needs no schema change and survives share links and reload.
proposal: J7 P5: children added from the book carry meta.book {type, section, name, partNumber}, and when the book's in-use price differs the row shows a quiet amber 'book: $1,140' chip that updates it in one undo frame. Hold the caveat hard — the chip must appear only on a real difference, or it becomes standing furniture on every book-sourced row. Largely makes G7's snapshot warning unnecessary.

title: The app cannot survive an offline reload
item: Everything edits fine offline, but a refresh gives a blank browser error page: there is no service worker and no web manifest, so the app is neither installable nor reloadable without a connection — and the book's offline message is written for a developer.
evidence: Offline: add-row, typing and totals all fine ($473.60 recomputed with no network); reload gives net::ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED at chrome-error://chromewebdata with an empty body and no #main-content. 0 service-worker registrations, no <link rel="manifest">, empty cache storage. The Assemblies side offline says 'Could not load mc-assemblies/mc-labor-book.json — serve the app locally.' (mcBook.js:383). Back online, the offline-added row was still there.
proposal: J11 P5: a minimal app-shell service worker (index, css, js, the five mc-assemblies JSONs) plus a web manifest, and a plain-words offline message. Two binding conditions from the verifier: it must never cache supabase.co or the jsdelivr CDN, so the 'zero network while signed out' property stays testable; and B13's Hard-reload rename must land with it, since only then does 'Hard reload' have a cache to clear.

title: There is no in-app account or password management
item: A tester is given a temporary password out of band and keeps it forever, because no change or reset path exists anywhere. And because the emailed code self-provisions, Manage Users is a directory rather than a gate — today's mix has the worst of both.
evidence: grep over js/ finds no updateUser and no resetPasswordForEmail, and the Edge Function exposes only create-user and delete-user (index.ts:49-66); index.html:165 is type="text" with no copy affordance. cloud.js:492 uses signInWithOtp({shouldCreateUser: true}), so any email address self-provisions an account. A promoted admin does not see their new surfaces until re-auth, because fetchProfileRole has exactly one call site, inside onAuthStateChange.
proposal: J13 P8, which the verifier correctly framed as a product decision the owner must make first: either make Manage Users the gate (turn off shouldCreateUser, so 'Add user' means something) or make it the directory it already is and drop the temp-password field entirely, letting the tester sign in with the emailed code. Either way, add a change-password path or remove the password path.

title: A promoted catalog part is shared back as the supplier's own price
item: Promotion marks a part userAdded, so the corrections diff emits it as a brand-new part carrying the supplier's catalog number — the shared book learns a catalog echo. And the quote history, which is the one thing worth sharing, is not in the shape at all.
evidence: Two promotions emitted kind:'new' corrections {labor:1.25, price:"106.29"} and {labor:0, price:"259"} — Elliot's own catalog prices, one with zero labor — and both survived a reload. The diff shape is exactly {tab, section, name, kind, old, new}: offers, history, priceSource and partNumber were each confirmed absent from a row that carried all four.
proposal: Open. The honest options are to exclude promoted rows from the corrections diff until a human quote lands on them, or to widen the shape to carry supplier and date so the admin panel can see who quoted what. Both change the J12 contract, so this is a product call rather than a queued fix.

title: The corrections loop has no return path
item: A contributor cannot learn what happened to their fix, and the shipping step is a hand-applied patch, a version bump, a commit and a deploy with no shipped marker anywhere in the data.
evidence: takeoff_suggestions.status exists per row and RLS lets a user read their own, but the list never shows it; downloadAcceptedPatch re-aggregates every accepted row ever (suggestionsReview.js:146-174). The pace itself was judged acceptable for a defaults book, provided the arrival is visible and the outcome is shown.
proposal: Deferred by design: T2-11 makes the arrival visible and B14 adds the shipped status, and the walker's own 'Pace' note says that with those two the pace is fine. Without them the pace is invisible rather than slow. Revisit only if the loop is used and the wait is what people complain about.
statusNote: Deferred: the return path is covered by T2-11 (the shared-book update notice) and B14 (the review queue), so a third surface would repeat them.

title: Zones of the book that no search reaches
item: T2-09 fixes the phrasing; this is the missing content behind it. The curated book is silent on every device query, and MAC adapters exist in the catalog with no labor figures anywhere.
evidence: 1900 box, single pole switch, pull string, toggle switch, occ sensor, photocell, disconnect 60a and romex all return zero curated hits (romex returns 56 Elliot rows and nothing else). 'mc connector' in MAC fill mode returns Assemblies 2 and Elliot Parts 43, and mc-labor-book.json holds 15 'MC CONN' rows — the parts exist, the labor does not.
proposal: A data task, not a UI one: grow the curated defaults for the device and MAC gaps, bumping LABOR_BOOK_DEFAULTS_VERSION so existing workspaces merge it. J5 P11's defaults-section half is warranted only for the labor figures the Elliot rows lack; the vocabulary half is already queued in T2-09.

title: No per-line taxable mark
item: T2-19 gives the rate a home and moves the sub-contract trench line, but a bid carrying owner-furnished material, a rental in one county and stock in another still cannot be expressed.
evidence: SALES_TAX_RATE is a constant and every material bucket is taxed; the verifier's counter-evidence was that rentals are taxable in many states and fill materials are genuine stock, which is precisely why a single global rule cannot be right everywhere.
proposal: Deliberately deferred: J8 P7's own caveat is that the teach half is a stop-gap and the per-line mark becomes the rework only if walks show most jobs carry trenching, and J5 P6's verifier said do not add a toggle. Revisit after T2-19 has been lived with.
statusNote: Deferred until T2-19 has been lived with — the per-project tax rate plus the untaxed site-work bucket may already cover the cases a per-line mark was asked for.

title: Assemblies cannot be edited, only replaced
item: A saved run recipe offers exactly two actions: load it, or delete it. Renaming one, fixing a single line of it, or seeing which runs used it are all impossible.
evidence: The assembly card's action set is 'Load into Ledger' and a trash, with a confirm on delete. Deleting does not mark the flow dirty and Cancel leaves without a guard.
proposal: Open. T1-09's per-run migration is the natural moment to revisit this, since the storage shape is changing anyway and legacy presets need a load path regardless.

title: No archive or close state for a bid
item: The project list only grows, so a season of bids makes the two most-used controls the farthest away. B11 makes the menu scroll; it does not make the list shorter.
evidence: At 24 bids the switcher menu is 919 px against a 900 px window with the footer at y 922, and the Manage modal's footer sits at y 1,190 inside an 810 px cap.
proposal: Raised in J10 F8 and deliberately kept out of J10 P6 by the verifier, who noted the archive idea is a separate proposal. Open.

title: The summary has no drill-down
item: An estimator with a calculator gets a different number from the app and has no way to ask where the app's came from, because the summary carries no explanation of any kind.
evidence: The summary block has 0 title attributes, no notes and no 'component/parent/rolled' text anywhere; the only sentence explaining parent-plus-component labor is B-11's line inside the devices flow, which stays because the flow needs it while editing.
proposal: J8 P6 failed the spirit test as written — a muted line is pure addition and removes nothing — so the verifier routed it to G8. A real UI shape would have to replace the bare hours cell text ('11.3 · runs 5.3 + parts 6.0') rather than add a row, and be re-tested against the four questions.

title: One feedback system
item: The app has no toast or live-region mechanism at all, so feedback is a native alert, a native confirm, a 1.2-second check swapped into a button, a status line the next render wipes, or nothing. Six journeys each patch their own corner.
evidence: grep -rn 'toast|aria-live' js index.html returns nothing. Observed in one pass: three distinct alert() texts on the import path; 'Please select a fixture...' as a page-blocking alert in the book; 'Remove this item?', 'Discard unsaved changes in this editor?', 'Delete "X"? This can't be undone.' and 'Remove the local Elliot price overlay?' as native confirms; a 1.2 s ✓ and a 1.5 s 'Copied!'; and #mc-elliot-status measuring empty right after a decision.
proposal: Open, and explicitly sequenced after the rows that need it: B4, B5, B10, B11 and T2-18 each replace one alert or one wiped status line. Standardising afterwards would retire all of them; standardising first would be a platform build with no consumer.

title: Picking a flow type yanks you into an eight-section editor
item: Labelling ten pasted rows drags the estimator into a full editor three times, and the only way back is the wordmark. Changing a flow row's type costs three clicks and parks its money in Misc in the meantime, because the picker cannot be reopened from a typed row.
evidence: modal.js:12-16 navigates on pick. .type-badge-flow is the only door into a typed flow row's editor (manifest.js:450-458); non-flow chips are listener-less spans; .select-type-btn renders only when item.type is null — so × then Add then pick really is the only retype route. Nothing is lost on the detour: clearing a Devices type keeps its children and re-typing shows them again.
proposal: J3 P2 failed the spirit test: routing every chip through the picker turns the daily one-click 'open my run' into two clicks to save one on a rare retype, and plants a modal in front of the affordance baseline B-2 installed. The shape the verifier proposed instead, and the one to build if this is taken up: keep the pencil as the direct one-click editor door, and make the chip's text (or a small caret beside it) open the picker with 'No type' at the bottom — one-click editor, two-click retype, and the × can go.

title: Delete is undiscoverable
item: There is no trash on a row by default, the one control shaped like remove removes the type instead, and the real route is four clicks behind a menu that closes on the toggle, so the checkmark recording the mode is out of sight.
evidence: TakeoffState.removeItem has exactly one caller app-wide (manifest.js:465). By default row 1 exposes book, ↳, × titled 'Remove type', minus and plus, with the trash not visible; #header-menu computes display:none immediately after the toggle. Clicking × moved $47.40 and 9.0 hrs into Misc.
proposal: J3 P3 (trash on row hover, always on touch widths, keep the confirm, drop the Remove-items mode and its menu row) passes the spirit test with two prerequisites the verifier made binding: T1-14 must land first, because a row-level trash that still no-ops on the icon makes the flakiness more visible rather than less; and an 'Undo' receipt is a real guard only once T2-03 lands, since the Undo button is dead after a keystroke today. Dropping the mode also removes showRemoveIcons from uiState.

title: The book has no second supplier
item: The provenance model already supports per-supply-house offers with an explicit 'in use' — that is one of this app's verified strengths — but the import side has exactly one vendor and tells you to edit a JSON file to add another.
evidence: The supplier select holds one option (Elliot Electric) with the hint 'Add suppliers by editing mc-assemblies/vendor-profiles.json'. The third search bucket is labelled with the vendor's name rather than what it is.
proposal: Open. T2-09's honest bucket labels ('Supply house · Elliot') are the cheap half and are queued; a second vendor profile end to end is a build.
statusNote: Deferred: needs a real second vendor's price file to design against. vendor-profiles.json already carries the shape; nothing is guessed until a file exists.

title: A keepalive-safe lid-close
item: The local flush at unload is solid; the cloud flush is not. beforeunload never calls the cloud's flushPending, visibilitychange is the only path, and no request uses keepalive — so the last queued push can die with the tab while the status shows a checkmark.
evidence: app.js:378-380 flushes local storage only; cloud.js:529-531 is the sole flushPending caller; no keepalive appears anywhere in the repo; signOut clears pushTimers without pushing (:507-514).
proposal: B13 makes the status honest, which is the cheap half. Making the push itself survive the tab is a separate build and is not queued.

title: No spec drives any of this
item: Three Playwright specs and a handful of node unit tests cover the data and almost none of the behaviour. Two of the Tier-1 blockers would pass every existing test, and one of them passes a spec that asserts success in the broken state.
evidence: No spec sets a viewport or calls tap(), so A-6, A-7 and C-11 have no regression test and nothing in *.test.js can cover them because layout is CSS. js/import.js, js/views/manifest.js and js/views/modal.js are IIFEs with no module.exports, so no *.test.js can reach parseCountToolingClipboard, inferType, handleFieldUpdate or the remove handler. labor-book.spec.js:20 asserts the assemblies status contains 'Elliot prices applied' and passes in T1-18's catalog-wiped state ('… 5,946 repriced, 0 new items'). elliotPriceCore.test.js exercises patchLaborBook only with non-empty newItems, so the else-branch behind T1-18 is untested. No spec opens #mc-elliot-modal, #users-modal, #part-card-modal or any flow editor; no unit test imports storage.js or cloud.js; the admin review panel has no test at all.
proposal: The dossiers name the specs to add, and each should ride the branch that makes it pass: a mobile.spec.js booting at 375×812 and 768×1024 asserting scrollWidth === innerWidth and that Add All and Load into Ledger are inside the viewport; a labor-book case per bucket asserting the child's price equals the price shown, plus a footage-parent quantity assertion; a describeBookRow unit for the shared bare names; the trash-icon-centre click; mergeDefaults(defaults, defaults) === 0; and a patchLaborBook case with empty newItems.
statusNote: Landed in the sense the row asked for: every fix in this program shipped with an automated check. At the close of the program the tree carries 21 Playwright specs (199 passing, 2 skipped) and 8 node:test files (167 tests), against the three Playwright specs that existed when the row was written. The two cloud round-trip specs are the skips: they need a non-admin test account in .env.local and migrations 001/003/004 applied.

title: Nothing measures anything
item: Listed last because it is the gap that makes every ranking above a judgement call. Takeoff Tooling has no logUserEvent equivalent and Supabase holds data tables only, so every journey is blind and 'high-traffic' in Tier 2 means 'on the daily core', not 'measured'.
evidence: Confirmed at frame time and re-confirmed by all fourteen walks: no telemetry of any kind; the Supabase project holds takeoff_store, takeoff_projects, takeoff_suggestions and takeoff_profiles, all data. Nobody knows whether a single estimator has ever opened this app on a tablet, how often the qty-0 rule fires on a real bid, or how many share links are opened.
proposal: Adopt Count Tooling's standing rule: every rework ships its own event. Each Tier-1 row above names one. The minimum useful first release is flow_saved, book_add_to_target, import_added, purchase_list_generated, pdf_exported, share_link_created, project_switched and a boot session_start {vw, coarsePointer}. Re-rank Tier 2 after one window of real data, exactly as Count Tooling did at its Stage-2 re-rank.
statusNote: Code landed (js/events.js + TakeoffEvents.log call sites, sanitized props, Do-Not-Track and an opt-out key). Migration must be applied: supabase/004_takeoff_events.sql. Until it is, events.js posts once, reads the 404, and stays silent for the session — the app is unaffected.

title: Boot
item: Pre-registered strength, verified. Synchronous restore from localStorage before first paint, under a second, fully offline, with no app-authored console error anywhere in the program.
evidence: 374–607 ms to a usable table. Across fourteen walks and fifteen verify passes the only console error in any context was the walks' own deliberately aborted Supabase CDN script (net::ERR_FAILED), and there were zero pageerror events anywhere.
proposal: Document as-is. X2's service worker must not disturb the synchronous boot.

title: Undo/redo on the manifest
item: Pre-registered strength, verified by unwinding the real stack rather than inferring frame counts.
evidence: One typing burst = 1 frame; two 1.4 s pauses inside a phrase = 3; three spinner clicks = 1; one frame per type pick, per import, per flow save; a parent removed with two children = one frame that restores the whole block; 60 alternating edits cap at exactly 50 (UNDO_STACK_SIZE, state.js:23/331). × then Add then pick inside 1.2 s collapses to one frame.
proposal: Document as-is. T2-03 and T2-04 fix the button state and the phantom frames around this core; the core itself is right and must not be touched.

title: The manifest card layout below 900 px — corrected
item: Pre-registered strength, and one of the two that needed correcting. It holds at iPad portrait and it does not hold on a phone, because one grid serves the whole 375–900 band.
evidence: At 768 px: nothing clipped, scrollWidth 768 = 768, every field labelled, grid 24 / 159 / 145 / 145 / 173 with every input inside its track. At 375 px the same grid clips a four-digit quantity and fuses Labor, Price and Plan Page (B12). Rotation to 1024 gives the desktop table at 976/976 with no horizontal scroll.
proposal: Protect the 768 px behaviour and the rotation flip. The wording of this strength must not be used to argue against B12's phone shape.

title: Import preview
item: Pre-registered strength, verified on an independent seed with the dollars checked: side by side, NEW badges, per-item deltas, counts treated as totals and never summed, one undo frame each way.
evidence: Delta text verbatim: '× 25 · now 18, +7' and 'already 10 — no change'. Add Overages Only raised 18 to 25 keeping $74.25 / 0.7 h intact: Lighting $2,516.50 → $3,036.25 (+7 × $74.25 exactly), 22.6 → 27.5 h. #import= works at boot and on hashchange with the hash stripped and window state intact; Esc and click-out both close.
proposal: Document as-is. T1-04 changes the buttons and T2-06 changes one delta string; the preview's shape is what they build on.

title: The provenance system
item: Pre-registered strength, independently re-derived on different parts and different supply houses.
evidence: Freshness tiers are exactly <30d fresh / 30–90d aging / >90d stale, verified at the boundaries (29 fresh, 30 aging, 90 aging, 91 stale, 100 and 365 stale) with the row badge and the card badge agreeing. First-quote-wins; a quote from a supplier that is not in use never moves the price; explicit Use copies price, source and date onto the row; offers merge case-insensitively; per-part history; offers, history, part # and labor all survive reload.
proposal: Document as-is. One exception is pinned in B6 (a promoted catalog part inverts first-quote-wins); the rest is a differentiator.

title: Purchase list — corrected to name its conditions
item: Pre-registered strength, and the second of the two that needed correcting: 'agrees with the summary to the cent' holds only under four conditions, each of which is now a queued row.
evidence: It merges by description, flags 'n without a price' instead of hiding gaps, keeps a run's footage and drops price-less groupings, and matched the Sub Total exactly on every clean seed ($11,273.51, $9,785.20, $7,806.15). It stops agreeing on a stale open list (T1-12), a priced qty-0 child (T1-05), a negative price (B9) and two 4-decimal supplier prices (B2). Copy produces clean TSV: header, materials sorted by description, a TOTAL row, no $ in cells, unit prices at two decimals.
proposal: Document as-is with the four conditions stated. The Copy TSV must stay bare when B2 adds thousands separators to the screen.

title: Fill mode
item: Pre-registered strength, verified. Any flow row's PB opens the book with the search focused and a banner naming the exact target; one click fills the row in place.
evidence: Banner verbatim: 'Fill: Back Box Support row 1 — selecting an entry replaces this row's description, labor, and price', with the search focused (baseline N-2 holds, with a complete section-label map). It is the only one of the four doors that focuses the search, and the only one that leaves a single, coherent row.
proposal: Document as-is. T2-08 keeps PB and removes the other doors precisely because this one is right.

title: Focus survives typing — corrected
item: Pre-registered strength, corrected in scope. True within a field everywhere — the panel and the summary are patched on input without a re-render, which is the hard part of this architecture — and true across fields in the conduit and wire flows. Not true across fields in the devices flow or on the manifest's labor rate.
evidence: Typing never loses focus in a description, a custom overage percentage (N-8 holds — the total line is patched in place) or any conduit/wire field; conduit.js:387/458 and wire.js:119 commit on blur without calling render(). The devices flow and the labor rate are T1-01, and J4's verifier explicitly killed the sub-claim that the conduit and wire handlers share the defect.
proposal: Document as-is with the scope stated. The wording must not be used to argue against T1-01.

title: The core count-to-total loop and its arithmetic
item: Added in Phase 2b. Every total on every route was correct to the cent when the inputs landed — across four dossiers, on seeds chosen so the hours did not fall on half-hours.
evidence: J8's sixteen hand-derived figures matched exactly: Lighting $2,607.50, Gear $981.85 (raw 981.8466), Sub Total $7,806.15, tax $663.52, 86.3 hrs, Labor $7,935.00, Grand $17,024.67. Also J1's $113.88 and $11,609.88, J4's $175.00 / 9.2 hrs / parent 8.0 + components 9.2 = 17.2, and J5's $5,025.58 conduit bucket verified line by line. The arithmetic is not this app's problem; the rules around it are.
proposal: Document as-is, and protect it: T1-05 and T2-19 change what is counted, not how it is computed.

title: The conduit wizard's quick-add and live overage line
item: Added in Phase 2b. One click on a trenching preset fills material, depth, price per foot and the run's own footage; the overage step computes live while you type and buys waste at the run's price with no labor.
evidence: Quick-add filled 150 / Dirt / 24in / 15 (baseline B-7 holds). Typing a custom 12% kept focus in the input for both digits and patched '150 + 18 additional = 168 total' live (N-8 holds). Overage priced at the run's unit price with labor 0 (A-2 holds): 27 × $0.68 = $18.36, 450 × $0.18 = $81.00. Exactly one overage child per run — replaced on re-save, never duplicated, and removed by a blank percentage.
proposal: Document as-is. T1-07's single-save rework and T1-24's write-time recompute must both preserve this behaviour exactly.

title: Step inference and exact hydration on re-entry
item: Added in Phase 2b. A run reopens at the step its children imply, and every field of every earlier step comes back exactly — including a blank price as an empty string rather than a zero.
evidence: Re-entering a saved conduit run landed on step 3 with '12' in the input and '220 + 27 = 247'; Back then Back hydrated the fittings and the trench fields exactly. The devices flow re-opened with all rows hydrated, blank seed rows for the empty sections, the CADDY row's blank price as "", and flowDirty false.
proposal: Document as-is. T1-07 must keep the inference when Next stops committing.

title: The devices flow's live rollup
item: Added in Phase 2b. The 'Job labor: parent 8.0 + components 9.2 = 17.2 hrs' line is the only place in the entire app that explains parent-plus-component labor — which is why G8 has to carry it in words.
evidence: Baseline B-11 verified: the panel is patched on every keystroke with blank rows excluded and no re-render, and the line correctly disappears on a parent with no labor. J8 found the summary has zero title attributes and no equivalent explanation anywhere.
proposal: Document as-is. J8 P6 was failed by the verifier partly because this line stays — the flow needs it while editing — so nothing here is removed.

title: The book's search core
item: Added in Phase 2b. Token-any-order matching with inch-mark normalisation, a filter that narrows curated and supplier rows together, a 100-row cap, open state surviving re-renders, and BOM expansion inside search results.
evidence: '3/4 emt coupling' and '3/4" emt coupling' both return 4 / 2 / 27 (A-4 holds); 'cplg' returns the same set; 'duplex receptacle 20a' returns 40 / 0 / 80+ via synonyms (N-1 holds). Tab-filter counts read 'First 100 of 759 matches', '1 match', '2 matches' (C-4 holds). One undo frame per single add and one per explosion (3 children → 0 → 3 on redo). Hotkeys work on both sides.
proposal: Document as-is, with the boundary the verifier drew: what is protected is the matcher and the one-frame-per-add, explicitly NOT the explode-by-default behaviour T1-02 kills.

title: The MC assemblies BOM footer
item: Added in Phase 2b. The footer states plainly what the app is doing about unpriced components, and it is the sentence T1-02 makes true.
evidence: Both variants correct on independent parts: '2 of 3 components unpriced — using the book price (4.03 hrs, $193.65)' and 'Computed per unit (book: 0.66 hrs, $42.52)' (baseline B-12 holds). Also C-9: the relabelled MC categories ('Adjustment units ($1 material · 1 hr labor)', 'Tenant Improvement budget rates', 'Grounding') are intact and correctly diagnosed.
proposal: Document as-is. T1-02 changes the add to match the footer, not the footer to match the add.

title: The part card
item: Added in Phase 2b. The card is the best-composed modal in the app and it is the one surface that already works on a phone.
evidence: Trail 'Gear · Transformers · 3PH' (B-9 holds); the record form, the offers table and the In use pill all readable. At 375 px it is 345×510 over the book with nothing past the right edge and no internal scroll needed (scrollHeight 508 = clientHeight), and Esc closes the card only, leaving the book and its open sections intact (B-8 holds — a section survived twelve quote records, six Use switches and the card's Close).
proposal: Document as-is. B6 fixes the ≤768 px desktop clipping and the trail's edges; the composition is not to be touched.

title: The share-link recipient path's mechanics
item: Added in Phase 2b. Everything about the recipient experience is right except the labor rate: no account, their own project, nothing of theirs replaced, and nothing on a server.
evidence: Lands in a project named after the sender with a '(shared …)' suffix (N-3 holds), rows and children intact with every quantity, labor and price identical, persists across reload, works at 375 px, and the recipient's own bids are untouched. The fragment never reaches the server — the site is static — so the whole bid stays in the two browsers.
proposal: Document as-is. T1-15 adds one field to the envelope and B10 adds a banner; the mechanics stay.

title: Project switching, duplicating and deleting
item: Added in Phase 2b. Every manifest round-tripped exactly through switch, duplicate, delete and reload, with correct undo semantics.
evidence: Switch restores rows, children and the per-bid rate exactly and clears undo (no cross-bid undo, which is correct); duplicate is a deep copy that is independent immediately (99 on the copy, 30 on the original); delete removes the storage key and the index entry while dismiss changes nothing (8 → 8 keys on dismiss, 24 → 23 on accept); reload reopens the same bid.
proposal: Document as-is. One caveat is a queued fix rather than a flaw here: the copy re-uses the source's item ids, which is what makes T1-17's cross-bid write possible.

title: The local-first spine
item: Added in Phase 2b. No Save button and none needed — and, verified twice, no network to the cloud at all while signed out.
evidence: A 400 ms debounce with a beforeunload flush that survived edit-then-reload-in-the-same-tick and edit-then-real-tab-close in both the walk and the verify pass; full editing offline with totals recomputing ($473.60); the legacy migration naming its project from its own date ('Takeoff — Jul 14') and leaving takeoff-workspace intact as a backup; and in the CDN-loaded observation context, one CDN script load and zero requests to *.supabase.co, with no sb-* keys written. A renderer kill inside the 400 ms window loses that edit — a design fact, recorded so it is not rediscovered.
proposal: Document as-is. T2-15 and X2 must not disturb any of it — in particular the service worker must never cache supabase.co or the CDN, so the zero-network property stays testable.

title: The merge semantics of the shared book
item: Added in Phase 2b. The rule that a user's own edits win while untouched rows follow upstream was verified row by row against the real defaults, and the corrections payload carries no job data whatsoever.
evidence: Seeded pre-boot at defaultsVersion 1: an untouched stale row took the new default (3.9 → 5.6), an edited row survived against it (12.4 against a default of 10.8), a removed row was not resurrected, a userAdded row was kept, an untouched row upstream had dropped left with it, a missing default was added, and the meta advanced — with a second boot byte-identical. computeCorrections has no manifest parameter at all, and dumping the keys of a correction whose row carried offers, history, priceSource and partNumber confirmed none of them travel. Opt-in defaults to Off and opt-out deletes.
proposal: Document as-is. T1-20 fixes the one datum that breaks the model (a duplicate name) and T1-26 fixes the path that skips the merge; the semantics themselves are sound.

title: The role gate
item: Added in Phase 2b. Signed out, none of the three admin surfaces render — and the supplier tool needed a declared test bypass to open at all.
evidence: Signed out the header menu renders exactly four items (New Project, Export via link, Remove items, Hard reload); #review-suggestions-btn and #manage-users-btn carry hidden with computed display: none (A-5's two rules holding), and #mc-elliot-update-btn is hidden via .btn[hidden]{display:none!important} (B-10 holds). The gating was measured before any bypass in both dossiers.
proposal: Document as-is and add the Playwright assertion J13 P6 asks for, so this class of bug stays dead. T2-01's base [hidden] rule strengthens the same gate rather than replacing it.

title: The supplier matcher's speed and its recovery hatch
item: Added in Phase 2b. The thing the supplier tool is for is fast and correct; what fails is what it does with the result.
evidence: 34,099 rows parsed (33,177 unique) and 5,692 items matched in 670–883 ms behind a correctly styled gold progress bar (C-3 holds), with every price rendered to C-1's decimal rule (0 of 300 review rows and 0 of 900 option labels showing float noise). 'Remove overlay' genuinely restores all 13 sections / 27,556 parts and the original 2026-07-18 import date.
proposal: Document as-is. T1-18's guard belongs in patchLaborBook, not in slowing the match down, and the recovery hatch must keep working — while telling the truth about the review queue it also deletes.

title: The type modal on touch
item: Added in Phase 2b. Its six option buttons are the app's only deliberately finger-sized targets besides one book button, and it is the model B12's coarse-pointer sizing should copy.
evidence: The six type buttons measure 194×44 at every width, and the modal scrolls internally at 664 px tall (615 > 596). Three exits all work with the type left unset — Cancel, Esc and click-outside (C-5 holds) — and the hotkeys are case-insensitive.
proposal: Document as-is. B12 should reuse this and .labor-book-add-btn's existing 44 px idiom rather than inventing a second sizing convention; B5's modifier guard (Meta+C must not pick Conduit) does not change the sizing.
